title: Tahun Yubileum Sebagai Hero (Hope, Efficacy, Resilience, Optimism): Sebuah Perspektif Psikospiritual
abstract: The Jubilee Year is a religious tradition that has deep meaning for Catholics, seen as a moment of grace that emphasizes liberation, forgiveness, and renewal of life. From a psychological perspective, this celebration not only functions as a spiritual ritual, but also as a coping mechanism that strengthens psychological well-being. This study aims to explore the meaning of the Jubilee Year through the HERO (Hope, Efficacy, Resilience, Optimism) framework, emphasizing how these psychospiritual dimensions are present in the experiences of the faithful. The research method used was qualitative, involving in-depth interviews with three informants who are active in spiritual communities and have undergone the Porta Sancta pilgrimage, as well as a literature review to strengthen the analysis. The data were analyzed interactively through reduction, presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results of the study show that hope is understood as spiritual energy that encourages the faithful to make peace with the past and move towards the future; self-efficacy is reflected in the belief that prayer, devotion, and concrete actions can strengthen self-confidence in the face of challenges; resilience emerges in attitudes of surrender, humility, and forgiveness that help the faithful rise from difficult experiences; while spiritual optimism is seen as the power of faith that fosters a vision of a future full of love and justice. Overall, the Jubilee Year becomes a psychospiritual space that strengthens HERO capital, making this celebration not only a liturgical tradition, but also a means of character building and resilience in facing the dynamics of life.

title: Remembering Gandhi and Rediscovering Humanity: Gandhi Jayanti 2026
abstract: Usually, the celebration of Gandhi Jayanti in India takes the form of a national observance, marked by official ceremonies in which the President, Prime Minister, and other leaders pay floral tributes and offer prayers at Gandhiji’s memorial at Raj Ghat, New Delhi. Government offices, schools, and banks remain closed. Gandhi Bhavans and other Gandhian institutions across the country organise prayer meetings and commemorative programmes. His favourite bhajans, ‘Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram’ and ‘Vaishnav Jan To’ are sung, while statues and portraits of Gandhi are garlanded.

title: War Is a Force That Gives Us Meaning
abstract: Drawing on the literature of combat, from Homer and Shakespeare to Erich Maria Remarque and Michael Herr, Hedges argues that human beings are conditioned to embrace what he calls "the myth of war"--The idea that combat is noble, selfless, and glorious, and yet, if human history is any guide, nations and imperiums have stumbled and even fallen when they believed the myths peddled about war and about themselves. The reality of war, asserts Hedges, with first-hand experience, is about the destruction of culture, the perversion of human desire, and the embrace, ultimately, of death over life.

title: Mutua Concordia: Enhancing the Responsibility of the Synod of Bishops of the Eastern Catholic Churches
abstract: Mutua concordia, an Apostolic Letter issued by Pope Leo XIV motu proprio on August 29, 2026, introduces modifications to Canons 106 and 126 of the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (CCEO 1990). These modifications strengthen the role and responsibility of the Synod of Bishops of the Eastern Catholic Churches. It gives the Synod greater responsibility in situations where the Patriarch or Major Archbishop fails to fulfil his duties. It provides the Synod with the authority to convoke the Synod when the Patriarch or Major Archbishop fails to do so. Furthermore, when there is a serious cause, the Synod is empowered to proceed, according to the norms and procedures established in the document, toward the removal of the Patriarch or Major Archbishop from office.

title: The Readout Condition: Distinguishability, Access, and Epistemic Warrant
abstract: Claims routinely distinguish more finely than the access sources invoked on their behalf. The central epistemic problem is not merely whether the resulting claim is true or justified, but whether each distinction in it is correctly attributed to the source, model, background evidence, relevance restriction, or decision rule that actually supplied the discrimination. This paper develops the Readout Condition as a necessary architecture for source-relative epistemic warrant. Its core is a threepart norm: existence (every claim-level distinction has an epistemic provenance path), attribution (a distinction credited to a source must be licensed by that source), and disclosure (essential augmentations must remain visible to audit). In the exact functional case, source attribution requires constancy on readout fibers and hence factorization through the readout. For non-transitive indiscriminability, the correct extension is pointwise: a claim token at an actual alternative is licensed only if its local indiscriminability neighbourhood lies inside the claim-value fiber, avoiding an illicit transitive closure. In stochastic settings, Blackwell garbling provides an access audit but cannot by itself detect assumption-driven silent lifts; a complementary identification ladder tracks the weakest augmentation layer at which a distinction becomes identified. The resulting typed provenance DAG supports a defeater-routing result: source-specific defeaters propagate exactly along the distinctions that depend on that source, while misattribution misroutes defeat and correction. Classical and pre-modern pressure tests from Dignāga–Dharmakı̄rti, Madhyamaka, Avicenna, and Suhrawardı̄ constrain the framework's neutrality. The proposed contribution is not a new factorization theorem, data-processing inequality, or general notion of provenance, but a unified distinction-level architecture linking access, identification, attribution, disclosure, and epistemic revision. Independent Scholar, Bangkok, Thailand. August 2026. Preprint — not peer reviewed. The Readout Condition is a standalone philosophical extraction from the public Readout Universe programme (github.com/morrocwi/readout_universe).

title: Walking with the Courageous Suffering Servant Jesus: A Johannine Perspective
abstract: John’s powerful presentation of the passion and death of Jesus brings out not merely the suffering servant but the courageous suffering servant Jesus. After deliberating upon the violent and voluntary death of Jesus, the article highlights the unique Johannine understanding of the glorification of Jesus. That suffering is glory/glorification is a specific perspective John has emphasised in portraying the passion of Jesus. Jesus’ suffering is value-oriented and courageous suffering, which is focussed here by contemplatively going through some of the key events of the passion narrative of John.

title: The author portraits in the Bedford Psalter-Hours: Gower, Chaucer and Hoccleve
abstract: AN inscribed portrait of John Gower, literary champion of Lancastrian kingship, provides the key to the reading of the unique illustrative programme of the Duke of Bedford's Psalter-Hours, Add. MS. 42131, the only manuscript he is known to have commissioned in England. Two hundred and ninety of the 300 minor text divisions are illustrated with portrait heads; a national portrait gallery of Lancastrian friends and foes is concealed in the initials of carefully selected texts. Many of the portraits are repeated, creating distinct subtexts; Gower himself appears ten times as prophet, preacher, and penitent lending the weight of his moral authority to the imagery. The depiction of contemporaries within the text of the Psalter is almost without precedent in the Middle Ages; the exception is in a Bible which was probably made for the Duke's father, Henry IV, by the artist of the inscribed portrait of Gower. This invasion of scriptural text defies convention and, it might be argued, good taste.

title: Fabricated citations: an audit across 2·5 million biomedical papers
abstract: Scientific literature depends on the integrity of its references. Each reference implicitly asserts that a verifiable source exists and supports the claims being made. When references point to non-existent studies, readers, reviewers, and policy makers are unable to evaluate the evidence.

title: A. T. Thomas
abstract: A. T. Thomas (1951-1997), a Hazaribagh Jesuit, witnesses to Jesus through his social action among the Dalits of Hazaribagh. Like Jesus, focusing on liberation, he serves the marginalised communities. His martyrdom reveals liberation (aphesis) as the heart of Christian discipleship, making visible God’s saving presence among the poor and inspiring continued commitment to justice, equality, and the transformation of society.

title: Baked Clay Figurines and Votive Beds from Medinet Habu
abstract: This catalog presents the entire corpus of 272 baked clay figurines and votive beds excavated at Medinet Habu by the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago during their 1926-1933 campaign. The figurines represent women, women with children, men, deities, and animals. They date from the sixteenth century B.C. to the ninth century A.D., illustrating permanence and change in themes of clay figurines as well as stylistic development within each type. The group of votive beds and the stela made from votive bed molds is among the largest and most diverse collections of such material. Each object is fully described and illustrated and is accompanied by commentary on construction, symbolism, and function.

title: The Presentation of Maat: Ritual and Legitimacy in Ancient Egypt
abstract: This work studies the relationship between the king and Maat, the personification of truth, as documented in reliefs of the New Kingdom and Third Intermediate Period. It includes a detailed study of the chronology, iconography, and theology of the ritual of offering Maat and the royal name equated with Maat. Central to the volume is an investigation of the construction of, and variations in, the offering formulas and what modifications in those texts reflect about the status of the king and about the relevance of Maat to ethics in the Ramesside period.

title: Paper13_ARI-Based Post-Cloud Preservation and Reference Infrastructure
abstract: This paper develops ARI-based post-cloud preservation and reference infrastructure for AI and AGI environments. It addresses the need for provider-independent reference continuity across documents, code, media, conversations, institutional records, evidentiary references, economic reference objects, and physical-digital contexts. The framework does not define a cloud replacement product, storage service, execution platform, evidence-confirmation system, legal archive, settlement mechanism, or provider-control system. Instead, it defines a structural preservation and reference layer through which records and outputs can remain human-readable, machine-referable, and institutionally traceable across multiple AI providers, platforms, models, and infrastructures. This paper follows the structural operating framework and provider-independent reference-layer foundation established in Papers 11 and 12, and extends the series toward long-term post-cloud preservation, public and institutional continuity, and reference infrastructure for AI-mediated environments.

title: Assessing intercultural communicative competence in virtual environments: Vietnamese EFL teachers' perceptions of assessment criteria
abstract: This study examines Vietnamese tertiary EFL teachers’ perceptions of assessment-relevant abilities and behaviours for digital intercultural communication competence (DICC) in virtual environments. Drawing on a teacher-only subsample of 197 participants from universities across Vietnam, the study used a 30-item questionnaire covering five dimensions: Intercultural communication readiness, contextual sensitivity, virtual interactional competence, reflective adaptability, and operational performance. Descriptive statistics and Cronbach’s alpha were used to analyse perceived importance, response variation, and internal consistency. Findings showed stronger endorsement of respect, openness, contextual sensitivity, polite and clear language, communicative adjustment, and culturally appropriate disagreement, while confidence, participation, explicit reflection, sensitive-topic management, and broad collaboration were relatively less salient or more variable. The results suggest that teachers conceptualise assessable virtual ICC primarily as relational, context-sensitive, adaptive, and behaviorally observable competence. The study highlights the need for contextually grounded, multimethod assessment criteria in Vietnamese tertiary EFL education and offers directions for future assessment framework development.

title: GenAI and Academic Writing
abstract: This paper exposes some of the main problems of cowriting with General Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) based on author’s experience of editing Springer Nature’s Postdigital Science and Education journal, Postdigital Science and Education Book Series, the Encyclopaedia of Postdigital Science and Education , and Chapters in Education. The paper outlines the four main challenges in facing scholarly editors—the challenge of detection, the challenge of sourcing, the challenge of writing, and the challenge of attitude. It reveals the opacity and practical uselessness of publisher guidelines, followed by some examples of methodologically and ethically sound human–GenAI cowriting. While presented conclusions are developed within the context of one publisher and its several publishing outlets, they are to an extent generalizable to contemporary academic publishing at least in the humanities and social sciences. The paper ends with an announcement of a zero-tolerance policy towards any kind of fraudulent human–GenAI cowriting in Postdigital Science and Education journal, Postdigital Science and Education Book Series, the Encyclopaedia of Postdigital Science and Education , and Chapters in Education, followed by an invitation for a broad postdigital dialogue about the future of academic writing with GenAI.

title: Accumulation of stranded plastic objects and other artefacts at Inaccessible Island, central South Atlantic Ocean
abstract: During 1987 a survey of macro-artefacts (>10 mm diameter) was conducted along a 900 m boulder beach at the western point of Inaccessible Island, central South Atlantic Ocean. This repeated the survey made at the same site during 1984, when the highest density of artefacts at the Tristan da Cunha/Gough and Prince Edward island groups (apart from Tristan settlement) was recorded at Inaccessible Island. The minimum rate of artefact accumulation was 88 objects km-1 year-1. Total numbers of artefacts had increased by47 per cent, with the greatest increase among plastic objects (65 %). Artefacts attributable to the local fishery were little increased in abundance, whereas those derived from distant sources had increased by at least 120 per cent, suggesting a recent increase in the density. of artefacts adrift in the South Atlantic Ocean. Published in: S. Afr. T. Nav. Antarkt., Deel 18, No. 1, 1988

title: UPAMANA PRAMANA IN SUSHRUTA SAMHITA NIDANA STHANA: A TAXONOMIC AND MORPHOLOGICAL STUDY
abstract: The Nidana Sthana of the Sushruta Samhita is a foundational text in Ayurvedic diagnostics that extensively utilizes Upamana Pramana (analogies and similes) to elucidate complex clinical and surgical concepts. To systematically decode this pedagogical framework, this conceptual article presents a comprehensive textual review of all 16 chapters of the Nidana Sthana, meticulously tabulating the utilized Upamanas, their specific clinical contexts, and the corresponding shloka numbers. The compilation reveals that Acharya Sushruta employed a diverse array of real-world imagery as precise diagnostic tools rather than mere poetic flourishes. The findings categorize these analogies into distinct domains: botanical and zoological imagery for soft-tissue lesions (e.g., comparing hemorrhoids to plant shoots), household physics for systemic failures (e.g., likening dropsy to oil seeping through an unbaked clay pot), and structural metaphors for anatomical deformities (e.g., mapping bone fractures to crab pinchers). Ultimately, this compilation demonstrates that bridging the gap between abstract human pathology and familiar natural phenomena provided ancient practitioners with an intuitive visual roadmap. For contemporary Ayurvedic scholars and clinicians, analyzing these ancient metaphors not only deepens the understanding of surgical pathology but also highlights a timeless pedagogical model for clinical education.

title: John Locke, Thomas Sydenham, and the Authorship of Two Medical Essays
abstract: Two medical essays in the hand of John Locke survive amongst the Shaftesbury Papers in the National Archives (National Archives PRO 30/24/47/2, ff. 31r-38v and ff. 49r-56r). Since the 1960s their authorship has been disputed. Some scholars have attributed them to the London physician Thomas Sydenham, others have attributed them to Locke. Detailed analyses of their contents and the context of their composition provide very strong evidence for Lockean authorship. This is reinforced by the application of the most recent techniques of computational stylistics.

title: The mediating role of emotion regulation in the link between enjoyment, anxiety, and emotional disengagement in multilingual learning: a response surface analysis
abstract: While recent second language emotion research has increasingly examined foreign language enjoyment (FLE) and foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA), most studies treat them as separate predictors, leaving unclear how their combined patterns link to emotional disengagement (ED) via emotion regulation. To address this gap, the present study examined how congruent and incongruent combinations of FLE and FLCA relate to cognitive reappraisal (ERCR), expressive suppression (ERES), and ED among multilingual international students in China. Data from 656 international students were analyzed via response surface analysis and mediation analysis. The findings reveal that distinct FLE-FLCA configurations correlate with divergent patterns of ERCR, ERES, and ED: ERCR is more pronounced when FLE outweighs FLCA, whereas ERES prevails when FLCA exceeds FLE; ED is minimised at the configuration of relatively high FLE paired with low FLCA. Further, mediation analyses confirm that ERCR and ERES mediate the link between FLE-FLCA configurations and ED, with ERCR exerting a more robust mediating effect. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that multilingual learners’ classroom functioning depends not only on individual emotions in isolation, but also on the coexistence and regulation of positive and negative emotions.

title: AN AYURVEDIC GUIDE TO THE DAILY CLOCK
abstract: If you look at a typical modern morning, it’s a masterclass in sensory overload. We jolt awake to digital alarms, immediately consume a flood of information from our screens, and rush out the door, which is physically fed, but energetically depleted. Thousands of years ago, Ayurvedic medicine proposed a radical alternative: Dinacharya(daily routine). This foundational framework for daily routine suggests that the very first choices we make upon waking don't just manage our time; they set the physiological and neurological tone for the entire day. The foundational principles outlined in Ayurveda texts, explains about how aligning daily actions with natural rhythms can effectively cut through the heavy, stagnant qualities of Kapha dosha that often manifest as morning lethargy. By contrasting modern habits with traditional practices including waking up in Brahma Muhurta, engaging in sensory cleansing, and grounding the nervous system through Abhyanga (body massage with medicated oil). These practices provides a roadmap for transforming chaotic mornings. Ultimately, it offers an accessible, scalable approach to integrate these ancient rituals, to build a sustainable foundation for lasting resilience, improved digestion, and balanced energy.

title: Paper 17 — Terms of Structure and Traceable Document-State Layers: Structural Conditions for AI+AGI-Generated Documents in the AGI Era
abstract: This working paper introduces Terms of Structure and Traceable Document-State Layers as a non-executive structural framework for AI+AGI-generated documents, document-state records, revision histories, structural conditions, and reference continuity. Building on the AGI Structural Alignment Series, this paper addresses how documents and document-derived outputs may remain traceable across AI+AGI generation, human review, revision, state preservation, publication readiness, institutional circulation, and long-term reference contexts. The framework does not treat document-state layers as contract terms, legal-effect mechanisms, execution systems, approval systems, evidence-confirmation systems, settlement systems, or automated decision systems. Terms of Structure are defined as structural conditions attached to document-state units, candidate outputs, revision units, role references, authority-condition references, time-history references, propagation boundaries, and preservation contexts. They may indicate reference status, review status, candidate status, preservation status, boundary status, or publication-readiness status without creating legal obligations or external effects. The paper positions traceable document-state layers as reference structures for maintaining continuity among generated text, human revisions, comments, tables, figures, code excerpts, media references, consent candidates, economic references, design references, and time-history records. The purpose is to preserve interpretive structure and non-substitution boundaries while keeping human and institutional discretion outside the document-state layer. This working paper is Paper 17 of the AGI Structural Alignment Series.

title: Publications proscribed by the Government of India: a catalogue of the collections in the India Office Library and Records and the Department of Oriental Manuscripts and Printed Books, British Library Reference Division
abstract: The books, pamphlets, periodicals, newspapers, handbills and posters proscribed by the British government in India are an invaluable printed archive for the study of the Indian freedom struggle during its last four crucial decades from the 1910s to the 1940s. As such they also constitute perhaps one of the largest accumulations of primary literature and ephemera relating to any twentieth-century independence movement. Four large collections of Indian proscribed publi­cations have been preserved. Two are in London, at the India Office Library and Records and in the Department of Oriental Manuscripts and Printed Books, British Library Reference Division, and two are in New Delhi, in the Library of the National Archives of India and in the files of its Home (Political) Proceedings. Smaller collections are to be found in at least some of the Indian state archive offices, such as that of West Bengal in Calcutta, and the Center for Research Libraries, Chicago, holds a complete microfilm copy of the personal collection of Professor N.G. Barrier (about a quarter the size of any of the major collections) made by the South Asia Micro­form Project (SAMP).

title: A major monastic centre? Rethinking Lismore’s place in the ecclesiastical landscapes of early medieval Britain
abstract: Until recent decades, the monastery of Lios Mòr (Lismore) in Argyll, Scotland, established by Saint Mo Luóc in the sixth century, was attested only via historical references and local traditions. Community-led investigations have now revealed an early medieval cemetery, sophisticated craftworking of international importance and early structures around the island’s parish church. These discoveries underscore the site’s status as a high-ranking ecclesiastical centre of the Insular north-west and elucidate its significance and integral role within the early Christian networks of Dál Riata, offering insights into the material traces of early medieval monasticism in northern Britain in the first millennium AD.
venue: Antiquity

title: Multimodal GenAI-assisted instruction in EFL argumentative writing: effects on writing skills, creativity, and critical thinking
abstract: With the rapid development of GenAI, multimodal instructional materials have become increasingly relevant to EFL argumentative writing because they can provide learners with richer input for idea generation and argument construction. However, limited studies have examined how multimodal GenAI-assisted instruction influences EFL learners’ argumentative writing skills, creativity, and critical thinking. To address this gap, the present study conducted a six-week instructional intervention involving two groups of Chinese EFL students, with 36 students in the experimental group and 35 in the control group. Quantitative data were collected through argumentative writing tasks and questionnaires, while qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews. The quantitative findings showed that multimodal GenAI-assisted instruction significantly improved students’ writing complexity, creativity, and critical thinking, although its effects on writing accuracy and fluency were not significant. The qualitative findings further revealed that students perceived multimodal GenAI-generated materials as useful for stimulating idea generation, broadening perspectives, enhancing analytical thinking, and supporting argument construction. These findings provide pedagogical insights into the use of multimodal GenAI-assisted instruction to support both writing development and higher-order thinking in EFL argumentative writing contexts.
venue: Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching

title: Carnivore scavenging patterns in terrestrial contexts: a 25-year retrospective study of forensic anthropology cases from Greece
abstract: Abstract Animal scavenging is frequently encountered in forensic investigations. The identification of scavenging is crucial, as scavengers have the potential to disrupt forensic contexts significantly by disarticulating body elements and consuming portions of bone. Determining the anatomical areas more commonly affected by scavengers can assist in recognizing the presence of scavenging activity in forensic contexts. Past forensic cases, submitted to the Forensic Anthropology Unit of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens Medical School for analysis between 1999 and 2023, were analyzed. Of the 256 cases examined, 62 exhibited signs of carnivore scavenging, while 194 presented no such evidence. To evaluate the impact of scavenging on human decomposition, the data collected from these cases were analyzed and compared. This comparison aimed to identify and assess any statistically significant differences in preservation and environmental conditions between scavenged and non-scavenged remains. The results indicate that scavenging is more likely to occur in rural settings and areas characterized by low population density. A lower prevalence of upper limb bones was reported in cases exhibiting signs of scavenging. Furthermore, this study identified specific anatomical regions that are preferentially affected by scavenger activity. Given the relative scarcity of similar research in Europe, the present study provides valuable insights into scavenging patterns in Greece and the broader European context.
venue: International Journal of Legal Medicine

title: The Ritual Landscape at Persepolis: Glyptic Imagery from the Persepolis Fortification and Treasury Archives
abstract: There are, perhaps, no more contentious issues within the study of Achaemenid Persia than those surrounding its religion(s) and religious iconography. Owing to the role that fire plays in Zoroastrian beliefs in later periods in Iran, almost any discussion of the subject of Achaemenid religion will eventually turn to the identification of sacred fire, fire temples, fire worship, and fire altars in the archaeological, epigraphic, and literary records. The focus of this book is a corpus of glyptic imagery preserved as impressions on two large archives of administrative tablets from Persepolis, the Persepolis Fortification archive (509–493 BC) and the Persepolis Treasury archive (492–457 BC). The glyptic imagery here published concerns representations of what have been traditionally termed “fire altars” and/or “fire temples.” Most of this glyptic evidence has never been published; many of the structures and the scenes in which they occur are strikingly original. The goals of this study are to introduce a new corpus of visual imagery concerning religious ritual in the Achaemenid period and to explore the significance of this visual language for our understanding of ritual traditions emerging within the heart of the empire at its most critical formative period, the reign of Darius I. This study seeks also to use the Persepolitan glyptic evidence as a springboard to re-visit the most famous “fire altar” depicted in Achaemenid art, that on the tomb relief of Darius I at Naqš-e Rostam. The glyptic images assembled in this study are the most numerous, the most visually complex, and the best dated and contextualized evidence that currently exists for the study of fire in ritual, and religious ritual more broadly, in early Achaemenid Iran. This study is also an initial step in the development of a religious topography for the zone encompassing Persepolis and Naqš-e Rostam, a topography that includes both images and the built environment.

title: The Imitation of Woman's Heart 1: Data
abstract: English and Chinese editions; audio and video at Sarah Chen Memory Gate. The album that significantly altered Sarah Chen’s career is the 1988 Woman’s Heart, her first collaboration with Jonathan Lee. Promoted as Lee’s new experiment, the album is often said to have launched a new “urban woman” phase of Chen’s career1. But was Woman’s Heart a Mandopop innovation? Or was it an imitation album? Here, using a data-driven approach, we analyzed the conceptual similarity between Woman’s Heart and Chen’s 1987 English album Miracle of Love. We showed that the six Lee-written songs on Woman’s Heart were highly similar to those on Miracle of Love. The finding challenges the album's originality. Rather than a new concept album, Woman's Heart is likely a Mandopop adaptation of Chen's English work. 【女人心效颦 1. 数据】陈淑桦的职业叙事在1988年发生了转变。她和李宗盛首度合作的《女人心》在宣传上走了「制作人至上」的路线,专辑被定位为李宗盛的新尝试,他以一个全新的概念开启了陈淑桦“都市女子”的阶段1。但《女人心》真的是华语乐坛的创新吗?它会不会是一部效仿专辑?本期以数据驱动的方法,分析《女人心》和陈淑桦1987年英文专辑《爱的奇迹》(Miracle of Love)的概念相似性。 分析发现,李宗盛填词的六首歌与《爱的奇迹》在统计上有极为显著的相似性,高于陈淑桦另外43首百代歌曲中任意六首歌的六百万种组合。这个发现对《女人心》的创新性提出疑问。虽然官方宣传说《女人心》是新概念专辑,但它更可能是陈淑桦英文作品的华语效仿集。

title: From Problem to Hypothesis: Dynamic Semantic Mobility, Bounded Knowers, and the Readout-Discriminable Hypothesis Space
abstract: Series. Paper I of the three-paper Bounded Knower sequence. Paper II: Knowledge Topology and the First Passage to Usable Hypotheses (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22307561). Paper III: Before Evidence Can Decide (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22307564). Paper IV: The Epistemic Chain Reaction (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22307751). Status. Bounded-knower final author draft under the Readout Universe / Readout Genesis architecture; GLOSA K0 — timestamped and citable, not independently reviewed, no priority claim. Claim tiers explicit: [definition], [Dr], [Open], [finite_diagnostic]. Produced with the glosa methodology (Rigour Without Infrastructure, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22301060); the founder's raw lines behind it are in the Blackbox Log (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22302518, e.g. entry BBL-2026-09-04-094 on imagination as reversible transport). Abstract. Scientific hypothesis generation is distributed across literatures on problem construction, abduction, analogy, model-based reasoning, semantic memory and control, insight, underdetermination, experimental discrimination, distributed cognition, and AI-assisted discovery. This paper proposes a readout-native architecture for the narrower domain of hypothesis-generating imagination. Its central thesis is that imagination can be modeled as bounded dynamic semantic mobility: not an infinite faculty and not a static set of reachable ideas, but a time-indexed process over semantic readouts whose transitions are provenance-audited, dynamically weighted, history-sensitive, and explicitly restructurable. Binary reachability is separated from graded accessibility; current constraints are typed by provenance so that forced distinctions cannot be silently erased while posited or borrowed constraints may be openly relaxed or retyped. Readout-semantic attraction and semantic momentum are introduced as finite access diagnostics, but they are explicitly separated from epistemic warrant and truth: a familiar or institutionally reinforced path may be highly attractive without being well supported. Candidate hypotheses are quotiented by reader equivalence under declared domain actions and a finite horizon, yielding a readout-discriminable hypothesis space. The framework further derives a bounded-knower corollary: epistemic standing is indexed by question, domain, time, reader, policy, and available records rather than inhering permanently in a person or social label. It also extends the architecture to collective epistemic systems without positing a group mind: shared records, artifacts, communication channels, and institutional policies define a collective semantic readout, attraction landscape, momentum trace, and warrant process. Three behavioral propositions remain central and falsifiable: attraction can invert into fixation, recent semantic paths can carry momentum into later search, and productive escape can occur through audited restructuring when a dominant basin fails to reduce residuals. A separate hypothesis concerning whether knowledge organization shortens expected time to a usable new hypothesis is deliberately reserved for a subsequent paper. The present manuscript remains a GLOSA K0 architecture pending independent review.

title: A Miscarriage of Revolution: Cameroonian Women and Nationalism
abstract: This article gives an account of Cameroonian women’s role in the radical, anti-colonial nationalist movement led by the UPC (Union des populations du Cameroun). Drawing on women’s petitions to the UN, one of the largest collections of political documents written by ordinary African women, as well as archival research and oral interviews, the article explains the formation of the Union democratique des femmes camerounaises (UDEFEC), a women’s political party linked with the UPC. The study demonstrates that the UDEFEC transcended ethnic, class, educational, and social divides, and popularized nationalism in both urban and rural areas throughout the Trusteeship Territories of Cameroon under French and British administration. By premising issues such as economic autonomy and biological and agricultural fertility, UDEFEC politics wove anti-imperial democracy into locally based political philosophies. More “womanist” than “feminist,” UDEFEC’s history sheds light on the essential components of women’s successful political mobilization in Africa, and contributes to the discussion of women’s involvement in nationalist movements in formerly colonized territories.
venue: University of Vienna

title: Study of Robustness Index and Product Index of Dry, Adult Human Clavicle in Bangladeshi population.
abstract: The clavicle is morphologically a modified long bone of upper limb and is also an important bone for transmission of body weight from upper limb to the axial skeleton, for muscle attachment and is a significant source of bone grafting. The basic framework of human body is reflected in bones and may provide valuable information about the biological identity of the deceased which can be used for forensic anthropological perspectives. Biological sex determination is one of the most important determinations to be made from human remains and is an essential first step in the development of the biological profile in forensics, anthropology and bioarcheology. The study which was descriptive cross-sectional in nature was done among 150 (65 right and 85 left) fully ossified and dried human clavicle in Mymensingh Medical College, Bangladesh from January 2020 to December 2020. Non-random purposive sampling technique was applied for sample collection from Department of Anatomy of Mymensingh Medical College and Community Based Medical College, Bangladesh, Mymensingh. The parameters were robustness index and product index; a ratio in which the baseline data were collected by the help of flexible measuring tape and rigid osteometry board. The robustness index is the percentage ratio between the mid clavicular circumference and straight length of clavicle whereas the product index is the inverse percentage ratio of robustness index. The mean ±SD robustness index of 65 right sided clavicles were 24.94±2.66 and 85 clavicles of left side were 25.02±2.41 whereas in case of product index it became 404.86±47.28 for 65 right sided clavicles and 403.29±38.77 for 85 left sided clavicles.

title: How multimodal GenAI enhances EFL learners’ language achievement: a parallel mediation analysis on the roles of psychological capital and emotion regulation
abstract: The incorporation of multimodal Generative AI (GenAI) into teaching is transforming how students engage with language beyond conventional text-based instruction. Although previous studies have examined the instructional benefits of AI-based language learning, less attention has been paid to the emotional and psychological mechanisms through which multimodal GenAI affects EFL learners’ language achievement. To address this gap, and drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study examines how multimodal GenAI improves EFL students’ language achievement through the parallel mediating effects of emotion regulation (ER) and Psychological Capital (PsyCap). Using a quasi-experimental design, 230 Chinese EFL students were assigned to either a GenAI-integrated experimental group using image-, text-, and audio-supported activities or a text-based control group. Over eight weeks, both groups completed curriculum-aligned language learning activities. Language achievement was measured using the Preliminary English Test (PET) as both a pretest and a posttest. The parallel mediation model showed that ER and PsyCap jointly mediated the effect of multimodal GenAI on EFL learners’ achievement. ER reflected students’ regulation of immediate emotional responses, while PsyCap captured enduring psychological resources that supported achievement. This study explains the dual emotional-psychological mechanisms through which multimodal GenAI supports EFL learning outcomes. These results offer theoretical and practical implications for designing cognitively supportive and psychologically empowering GenAI-based EFL instruction.
venue: Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching

title: The Despars Avicenna *Canon* Corpus: A Seven-Witness Substrate-Anchored Inventory (1431–1498)
abstract: This paper presents a substrate-anchored seven-witness inventory of Jacques Despars's commentary on Avicenna's Canon medicinae (Latin translation of Gerard of Cremona, c. 1170s), assembled inside a research substrate that tracks several hundred late medieval medical manuscripts, figures, and findings (substrate snapshot, June 2026) [Honeycutt 2025, Paduan Medical Reference dataset, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18687530]. Despars (c. 1380–1458), regent master of medicine at the University of Paris and physician to the houses of Burgundy and France, compiled his Commentarii in Canonem between 1432 and 1453 [1][2]. The seven-witness list is anchored by Jacquart's manuscript census, the Biblissima records for the BnF witnesses, and the BSB image record for the Lyon print [1][4][5][27]. Six manuscript witnesses are catalogue-anchored; the Lyon 1498 print, BSB Munich bsb00071249 volume three, is anchored at folio imagery level and has been HTR-walked at corpus scale. A thirty-two-folio handwritten-text-recognition (HTR) walk of that print, processed under Kraken with the CATMuS Medieval 1.6.0 model, returned raw hits across seven tracked Latin pharmacological class-words (paleographer verification pending) and is reported as an Observed pattern, not as closure on the seven-witness inventory [6]. The paper situates the witnesses against Padua scholastic medicine, catalogues them with source-bounded metadata, and supplies a tier and falsification matrix.

title: The Infinite Interior: On Space, Change, and the Integrity of the Self
abstract: This essay advances a structural account of identity through change by reframing space as the condition of transition rather than a passive container. It argues that every transition between states contains a continuous infinite interior—an asymptotically traversed distance that admits no boundary. Because replacement requires a boundary at which one state ceases and another begins, a continuous interior precludes replacement and preserves identity as continuous modification rather than succession. On this basis, the persistence of the self is not grounded in memory, material continuity, or narrative coherence, but in the topology of transition itself. The human self is understood as an irreducible unit that remains numerically identical through change by continuously traversing this interior at the point of actualization, the Now. The argument is developed through engagement with classical and modern accounts of identity and becoming, and concludes by examining the necessity of a sustaining ground that holds both temporal actualization and continuous transition open. Identity is thus preserved not despite change, but through it, as a consequence of the absence of ontological boundaries within transition.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Hartlieb *Kräuterbuch* 9-Witness Corpus: A Snapshot-Bounded Census
abstract: Johannes Hartlieb's Kräuterbuch (composed ca. 1435–1450) is a German-vernacular illustrated herbal of 173 chapters, attributed in the cited standard references in the modern scholarly record to Hartlieb (Grubmüller 1981; Hayer and Schnell 2010). The work survives in nine catalogued manuscript witnesses on the current Handschriftencensus record (Werk 2317, snapshot 2026-05-24) and no incunable witness is recorded in the cited census and search surfaces. This paper presents a substrate-complete census of those nine witnesses: five stand-alone copies (Berlin SBB Ms. germ. qrt. 2021; Wolfenbüttel HAB Cod. 79 Aug. 2°; Wien ÖNB Cod. 2826; Nürnberg GNM Hs. 18792; Schloss Anholt, Salm-Salm Ms. 46), three witnesses that embed Hartlieb's plant chapters inside Konrad von Megenberg's Buch der Natur (Heidelberg UB Cpg 311; Michelstadt Nicolaus-Matz-Bibliothek Cod. D 684; Erbach Gräfliches Gesamthausarchiv Nr. 2), and one fragmentary stand-alone witness (Linz OÖ Landes-Kultur Ms. 4). Each witness is presented on a common codicological axis. The census is cross-referenced with the wider Hartlieb authorial corpus, which the Handschriftencensus author-record autoren/421 enumerates as 103 werk-entries across approximately 93–99 unique codices once Sammelband-internal overlap is deduplicated. The paper then frames the Kräuterbuch corpus as a structural comparator for the herbal section of Beinecke MS 408 (the Voynich Manuscript) at the level of production ecology only, with no identity inference, and explicitly distinguishes this framing from the authorship hypothesis of Brewer and Lewis (2024), which the project record disfavors on content-side grounds set out in §6.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Weight of the Present: On Condensation, Grace, and the Continuity of Becoming
abstract: How does one moment of a being become the next without losing identity? This essay introduces condensation as the dynamic operation underlying the Gaitan Topology. Every present gathers rather than replaces the preceding state, preserving continuity through two inseparable principles: inheritance, by which identity endures, and reception, by which novelty, freedom, and grace become possible. From this operation arise trace, structural inertia, and the enduring orientation of the self. Drawing on Augustine, Aquinas, Bergson, and Whitehead, the essay argues that grace does not interrupt continuity but enters the condensation itself, reorienting the person without replacing the one who receives it. Condensation thus provides a unified account of memory, habit, absolution, and the final transformation of the person at death.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Wittelsbach–Burgundian Transalpine Physician Chain, 1413–1496 (with southern Frederician and northern print-tradition extensions)
abstract: This paper traces a transalpine court-physician chain whose Confirmed-tier coverage runs from the start of the Cermisone Padua professorship (1413) through the latest dated Generation-2 vernacular witness (1496), with Candidate-tier extensions to the Constitutions of Melfi (1231) at the southern end and the Upper-Rhine surgical print-tradition reception (1583) at the northern end. The keystone is Johannes Hartlieb's Padua doctorate of 11 May 1439 [1], anchored at scholarly-consensus level by Fürbeth's 1992 Untersuchungen zu Leben und Werk monograph (Hermaea NF 64, Niemeyer Tübingen, pp. 30–41), which links a Bavaria-Munich Wittelsbach court physician directly to the teaching faculty of Antonio Cermisone and Bartolomeo Montagnana. Around that keystone we read a nine-manuscript witness cluster (1429–1496) carrying iatromathematisches Hausbuch, Regimen sanitatis, and Speculum humanae salvationis calendrical material across a German-vernacular regional book culture spanning Bavaria, Bodensee, Konstanz, Heidelberg, and Bohemian-Silesian production sites [2]. At publisher/imprint level, the separately compiled Bolt corpus describes approximately 1,000 apothecaries in roughly 85 Burgundian-state towns between 1200 and 1600 [3]; the exact internal count of 1,029 remains unreproduced here. The Avicenna Canon (Gerard of Cremona Latin) supplies a 14th–15th-century textual spine, carried in this study by seven Despars-stratum manuscripts in our holdings [4]. The Burgundian–Wittelsbach extension section engages the Brewer–Lewis 2024 Social History of Medicine paper as a methodologically valued, peer-reviewed precedent that correctly identifies Hartlieb's Bavaria-Munich service but does not extend the Wittelsbach reading across the Bavaria-Straubing maternal-line dynastic bridge into the Burgundian court. The paper closes with a programmatic register of the corridor's unexploited cross-connections to the Doutrepont–De Winter–Wijsman–Falmagne–Vaughan Burgundian-library bibliography and to the Bolt apothecary corpus. The thesis is comparator-lens, not identity. We do not claim that the chain produced Beinecke MS 408; we claim that the chain is a substrate-anchored object whose members, dates, teacher–student edges, and manuscript witnesses are attested at primary-source or scholarly-consensus level (the keystone doctorate date at the latter; see the keystone date section) and bracket the relevant fifteenth-century medical-book economy with sufficient density to be read as a stratum in its own right.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Thermodynamics of Records
abstract: This paper develops an interpretive account of the physical life cycle of records within a consistency-history framework. Earlier papers in the series characterized a committed record as “decoherence- and thermodynamics-protected, append-only in practice.” The present paper refines and partially corrects that formulation. A physical record is not logically immutable or fundamentally append-only. It is revision-resistant in practice insofar as its information is encoded in sufficiently protected physical degrees of freedom, often—but not universally—through metastability and free-energy barriers. The central claim is structural and deliberately deflationary: there is no single thermodynamic price of a record. Record formation, passive retention, revision, logically irreversible reset, active error correction, and redundant proliferation are distinct processes with different, implementation-dependent demands. The paper therefore replaces a scalar cost with a physical record profile comprising resources, performance, and architecture: free-energy and dissipation budgets, control resources, operation and retention times, error rates, and an effective number of sufficiently independent carriers or access channels. Landauer’s principle directly constrains the logically irreversible reset component of this profile. Other record processes inherit a Landauer-type constraint only when their implementation contains a reset or another logically irreversible information-discarding step. The formation of a classical record is represented as the logically reversible, in-principle correlation of distinguishable pointer states with an initially prepared memory. This is not the cloning of an arbitrary unknown quantum state, and a complete reusable memory cycle must still account for preparation and reset. The paper further distinguishes logical commitment, physical durability, and public finality. Public finality requires an operationally significant redundancy of sufficiently independent, accessible, and durable carriers or access channels. This is an architectural requirement, not a universal additive heat cost per copy. Environmental amplification may generate redundant records without implying a universal Landauer-type price for each environmental fragment. The framework derives no result in thermodynamics or statistical mechanics. It does not derive the second law, the Landauer bound, any fluctuation theorem, the thermodynamic arrow of time, or the low-entropy boundary conditions of the universe, and it makes no independent empirical prediction. Its contribution is a disciplined decomposition of the physical processes through which records are formed, protected, revised, erased, maintained, and made publicly accessible.

title: Descriptive Opener-Class Structure in the Voynich Manuscript Balneological Section (f75r–f84v)
abstract: This successor retains the twenty-folio count table and four-zone description and adds the missing tie-sensitivity replay. Two folios are tied: f78r at q=11 and s=11, and f79r at q=10 and s=10. Across all four admissible tie resolutions, G ranges from 11 to 13 and the one-sided Monte Carlo permutation value ranges from 0.00048 to 0.02284 at 100,000 trials per configuration. The uniform-label null is therefore rejected at 0.05 under every tie resolution. This does not distinguish the proposed regimen from a another topically structured arrangement. The s-to-q-to-o-to-s treatment sequence remains Candidate and lacks an independent period-source witness. The balneological section of the Voynich Manuscript (f75r–f84v, 20 folios) has been read as bathing imagery, gynecological imagery, or an alchemical process. This paper reports a class-opener extraction over the identified IVTFF file and evaluates a four-zone rule defined in the Methods. Under the alphabetical tie rule, the script records G=13/20 against a 10,000-shuffle null (mean 6.13, SD 1.93, corrected one-sided empirical p=0.0007). The observed dominant-class sequence is: Zone 1, three s-dominant and one o-dominant folio; Zone 2, six q-dominant folios; Zone 3, three o-, two q-, and one p-dominant folio; Zone 4, one s-dominant folio followed by three q-dominant folios. These are script outputs under the internal class labels, not plaintext meanings. The f79v midpoint description and its figure labels come from the internal image audit and remain descriptive. A former working-note claim that Conciliator labels occur on all 20 folios is not retained. This packet contains no exported query receipt, detection threshold, or off-section base rate for that claim; P-004 and the Paduan dataset are program-context and priority references only. The partial image taxonomy assigns 12 of 20 folios to COMMUNAL POOL, CASE ENTRY, or CATALOG ROW categories and leaves eight unbucketed. The s→q→o→s phase interpretation is an internal workflow hypothesis situated in P-009's corridor context, pending an off-section baseline and an independent medieval-source locus for the proposed order.

title: Paper 21 — Public and Institutional Propagation and Preservation Boundaries in AI and AGI Environments: A Provider-Independent Framework for Record Circulation, Publication Readiness, and Long-Term Reference Continuity
abstract: This working paper develops a provider-independent framework for public and institutional propagation and preservation boundaries in AI and AGI environments. As generated outputs, document-state records, role references, authority-condition references, verification traces, time-history records, economic reference objects, domain design references, and physical-digital observations move across organizations and public contexts, the central problem is whether such records are structurally positioned for circulation, public reference, institutional sharing, archival preservation, or later review without being mistaken for official action, public disclosure, evidence confirmation, value transfer, legal effect, or institutional approval. The framework treats propagation as bounded reference circulation and preservation as long-term reference continuity. It does not publish, approve, transfer, decide, certify, settle, authenticate, grant authority, determine legal effect, or replace human and institutional discretion. The paper connects provider-independent structural reference layers, public-sector reference infrastructure, telecommunication edge reference nodes, essential-function parity reference hardware, traceable document-state layers, time-history and seal-reference structures, economic reference objects, domain design references, and post-cloud preservation infrastructure into a public and institutional boundary model. This working paper is Paper 21 of the AGI Structural Alignment Series.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Recurrence plots in linguistics
abstract: Abstract This paper illustrates the use of recurrence plots as tools for linguistic analysis. We emphasize their potential to kickstart research into un(der)studied languages or linguistic data, focussing on ways of using them that require little linguistic preprocessing, needing only an audio recording of speech or a transcription with or without gloss (the first level of linguistic annotation that field linguists create). Recurrence plots can offer insight into the repetition, and repetition-with-variation, structures of these (relatively) raw linguistic materials, thus offering first inroads into the internal composition of even little- or un-annotated data. As an example, we work with audio and transcriptions from Igu, a language used solely for ritual purposes in the Kera’a-speaking community of Arunachal Pradesh (India). We show that recurrence plots are useful in highlighting specific aspects of repetition in the materials analysed.
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics

title: Bongo Flava (Still) Hidden „Underground”1 Rap from Morogoro, Tanzania
abstract: Bongo Flava, the Tanzanian variety of HipHop has become a big issue in Tanzania during the past few years. More and more young people use rap lyrics to express themselves. This article first gives a brief overview of the history of Bongo Flava and discusses the topics, lyrics and the sound of this music. It then turns to the situation of the underground rappers with focus on the regional capital Morogoro. The second part of the article discusses selected parts of three songs that were written by Juma Madoweka, one of the young rappers from Morogoro who rap because they want to pass on a message to the society they live in.
venue: University of Vienna

title: Socio-Cultural Transformation among the Dhangar Community in Solapur District
abstract: including Solapur district. The Dhangar Community has always had a connection with pastoralism, sheep and goat rearing moving with the seasons traditional jobs, family relationships, cultural activities and groups that work together.. Over time the way of life of the Dhangar Community has changed because of new money situations, more learning, cities growing new tools being used the environment changing and new jobs becoming available. These changes have led to changes in the way the Dhangar Community lives and how they are organized socially and culturally. This study wants to look at the changes happening in the cultural way of life of the Dhangar Community in Solapur district. It pays attention to changes in family setups how people get married, family connections, what jobs people do what they hope to learn what roles men and women play, religious activities, celebrations, traditions what they eat what they wear and how they get along with others in the community. The study also wants to find out how the members of the Dhangar Community deal with traditions and new ways of living. The research will use a method that involves going into the field and getting first-hand information from interviews watching what people do filling out questionnaires and talking with some people from the Dhangar Community. Information from sources will help understand the past how many people there are, the social side and the culture of the Dhangar Community. The study will pay attention to differences between older people and younger people and to what happens in homes where people have changed jobs or moved away. This study expects to show that the changes happening in the Dhangar Community are not about giving up old ways or just taking on new ways. Instead these changes are about adapting and finding a way to mix traditions the way the community sees itself and new goals that people have for their lives. The study could help people understand more about how the lives of people who live by herding animalsre changing. It could also offer ideas for programs and plans, about learning, jobs helping people live better and keeping traditions alive in Solapur district.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Interior Design: Opportunities, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the design industry by introducing data-driven, generative, predictive, and automated approaches to creative and technical processes. Interior design, traditionally dependent on human creativity, spatial understanding, material knowledge, and client preferences, is increasingly influenced by AI-powered tools capable of generating design concepts, visualizations, layouts, material combinations, lighting solutions, and personalized spatial recommendations. Recent developments in generative AI, machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems have expanded the possibilities for designers to explore a larger number of alternatives in less time. This research paper examines the opportunities, challenges, and future perspectives associated with the integration of Artificial Intelligence into interior design. The study adopts a qualitative systematic literature review approach and synthesizes recent research on AI-assisted architectural and built-environment design. The review indicates that AI can support concept generation, space planning, 3D visualization, material selection, sustainability analysis, personalization, and client communication. However, issues related to creativity, algorithmic bias, intellectual property, data privacy, professional responsibility, design authenticity, technical skills, and overdependence on automated systems remain significant challenges. Recent systematic reviews show that AI research in design is strongly concentrated in early conceptual and schematic stages, while later stages requiring detailed technical, contextual, and professional judgment remain comparatively underexplored. The paper argues that AI should not be viewed as a replacement for interior designers but as an augmentation technology that can strengthen human creativity, decision-making, and productivity. A human-centred AI framework combining technological capability with professional expertise, ethical safeguards, cultural sensitivity, and user participation is proposed. The study concludes that the future of interior design will increasingly depend on effective human–AI collaboration rather than complete automation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Beckers Collection (Aachen) - Ushabti UB-014: Ushabti of Hori I (Tell Basta)
abstract: Faience ushabti of the Viceroy of Kush Hori I (UB-014) — Object documentation, Beckers Collection (Aachen) Small mummiform faience ushabti with whitish glaze and dark brown to purplish-brown painted details, produced for Hori I, Viceroy of Kush under Ramesses III and IV (20th Dynasty, c. 1150–1100 BCE), from the tomb of Hori I at Tell Basta (Bubastis). The object belongs to a closely defined series of small faience ushabtis documented in scholarship since Habachi (1957) and most recently surveyed by de Haan (2019). This record includes full object description, material and dating assessment, inscription analysis, comparative evaluation, provenance chain, and bibliographic references. Height approx. 10.8 cm. This version includes professional photographic documentation and UV fluorescence examination. This publication is part of an ongoing research-driven collection project, aiming at transparent, versioned, and citable object records.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Popular Music and Politics in Africa – Some Introductory Reflections
abstract: ‘Popular culture’ is a broad term, especially if the meaning of ‘culture’ is understood as referring to “[...] whatever is distinctive about the ‘way of life’ of a people, community, nation or social group.” (Hall 1997: 2) However, for the purpose of this collection of articles, a useful distinction is between cultural practices such as drinking, eating, sports, fashion or religion and those forms of popular culture which are, in a more narrow sense, artistic cultural expressions, encompassing different genres such as music, theatre, dance, visual arts and literature. As Barber (1997: 1) points out, music is the first form of popular culture in Africa which has been (noticed and) studied outside the African continent. (cf. Fabian 1997 [1978]: 18) The still rather strong focus on music in the study of popular culture is also reflected in this special issue which is almost exclusively dedicated to this genre.
venue: Phaidra (Universität Wien)

title: The Ground That Knows: On Grounding, Presence, and What Divine Knowledge Is
abstract: Previous essays established that God does not know through observation, reception, or any perfected form of finite cognition. This essay supplies the constructive account left intentionally deferred. Its central claim is that grounding and knowing are not distinct divine acts but two names for a single relation viewed from different perspectives. Grounding names the creature's dependence upon God for the actuality of every present moment; knowing names that same relation insofar as nothing occurring within the creature's present stands exterior to its ground. From this identity the essay derives a unified account of omniscience that no longer depends upon perception, attention, temporal succession, or inspection of a completed timeline. The familiar negations developed in earlier essays become positive consequences rather than isolated denials. The paper also addresses the principal theological objection raised by such an account—that immediate presence to the creature's interior entails pantheism—by distinguishing grounding from identity through the asymmetrical relation of continuous creation. The result is a constructive metaphysics of divine knowledge within the Gaitan Topology. Divine knowledge is not a cognitive faculty directed toward an independently existing world but the intelligible aspect of God's sustaining relation to creation itself. The essay therefore completes the transition from apophatic critique to positive ontology initiated by the preceding studies.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Rethinking The Paithani Handloom Economy In Maharashtra
abstract: Abstract Paithani is simultaneously a heritage textile, a livelihood system and a differentiated market product. This paper develops a new analytical framework for understanding the contemporary Paithani handloom economy in Maharashtra by connecting four dimensions that are often examined separately: cluster structure, production economics, market access and authenticity. The analysis is based on the supplied study of the Yeola and Paithan clusters and reorganizes its evidence into a business-oriented interpretation rather than reproducing its original structure. The source describes more than 12,000 active handloom weavers and auxiliary workers, annual production above 85,000 authentic handloom sarees, and a strong concentration of commercial activity in Yeola. It also identifies substantial differences between the cost of authentic handwoven products and powerloom imitations. The paper argues that the central economic problem is not simply competition from cheaper substitutes; it is the difficulty of converting craftsmanship, time and authenticity into a price that is transparent and understandable to consumers. GI protection, digital direct-to-consumer channels, traceability, raw-material support and design innovation therefore need to operate as a connected strategy. The paper concludes with a practical framework for strengthening artisan bargaining power while protecting the identity of Paithani.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The contribution of multimodal AI technologies to EFL teachers’ pedagogical effectiveness and perceived readiness for AI-mediated education: a qualitative study
abstract: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies can influence different aspects of teaching English as a foreign language (EFL). However, the way of adopting such innovations may affect teachers’ pedagogy and readiness for a new mode of education mediated by AI tools is left underexplored. To fill the gap, this study examined 40 Chinese EFL teachers’ perceptions about the contributions of multimodal AI tools to their pedagogical effectiveness and AI readiness. Interviews were held with teachers individually and online. Thematic analysis of the gathered data indicated that AI adoption could affect pedagogical effectiveness by making their instruction flexible and creative, reducing their workload and pressure, and fostering feedback and assessment practices. Furthermore, multimodal AI tools could affect teachers’ AI readiness by developing their AI confidence, competency, and literacy and inspiring their role shift and professional development engagement. Implications are provided for EFL teachers and teacher educators to enhance effectiveness and readiness for AI-mediated education through the integration of multimodal AI tools.
venue: Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching

title: Sustainable Futures and Literary Voices: Eco-Criticism in the Age of AI
abstract: Abstract: The accelerating climate crisis and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a new intellectual landscape in which environmental sustainability no longer be discussed independently of technological development. Literature, as a cultural form capable of representing ecological relationships, technological anxieties, and alternative futures, has an important role in this debate. This paper examines how contemporary ecocriticism respond to the environmental challenges associated with artificial intelligence while also exploring the potential of AI to support environmental knowledge, literary interpretation, and sustainable futures. Drawing upon ecocritical theory, environmental humanities, posthumanism, Indigenous ecological thought, and recent scholarship on AI and environmental sustainability, the study analyses selected works including Margaret Atwood’s Oryx and Crake, Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement, Richard Powers’s The Overstory, Robin Wall Kimmerer’s Braiding Sweetgrass, and Donna J. Haraway’s Staying with the Trouble. The paper argues that these texts challenge anthropocentric assumptions by foregrounding interdependence among humans, nonhuman organisms, technologies, and ecological systems. Atwood exposes the destructive consequences of technological mastery; Ghosh identifies the limitations of literary forms that marginalize ecological catastrophe; Powers expands narrative attention from individual human lives to forests and multispecies networks; Kimmerer proposes reciprocity rather than domination as the basis of ecological ethics; and Haraway advocates “making-with” other species rather than seeking technological mastery over nature.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The New Human Standing Canon v0.3: Standing Surface with Strong Entity Relations — Combined Set of Figures, Texts, and Lineages Declared into the New Human Canon by Effective Act

title: Building an Egalitarian Society and Sustainable Development: A Study of Dr. Ambedkar's Thoughts
abstract: Abstract: The concept of sustainable development is very important in modern times. In sustainable development, importance is given to socio-economic and environmental development. 17 goals have been identified to achieve sustainable development. While considering these goals, the sustainability of Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts is also being highlighted. His thoughts also reflect various aspects of sustainability such as poverty eradication, inequality eradication, good health and welfare, quality education, gender equality, and economic growth. The main objective of this research paper is to study how useful Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts are in this concept. Descriptive and analytical research methods have been adopted for the presented research paper. Also, secondary sources have been used as a source of information. When considered in the context of sustainable development, Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts are analogous to the goals of sustainable development. If sustainable development is to be achieved, it is possible to create an equitable, just, and inclusive society by keeping Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts in mind; therefore, Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts are as effective and useful today as they were then. Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts are still a guide for creating an egalitarian society. In the present research paper, when the goal of sustainable development and the thoughts of Dr. Ambedkar are studied, it is found that out of the 17 goals of sustainable development, Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts show similarity with 10 goals. Therefore, even in contemporary times, Dr. Ambedkar's thoughts are still guiding and useful for the welfare of society, for eliminating inequality in society, establishing economic equality, and preserving human dignity.

title: Paper 22 — Provider-Independent AI Civilization Infrastructure: A Human-Centered Structural Framework for Public, Institutional, Technical, and Physical-Digital Reference Continuity in the AI and AGI Era
abstract: This working paper presents a provider-independent framework for AI civilization infrastructure in a strictly structural sense. The paper defines AI civilization infrastructure as the public, institutional, technical, and physical-digital reference conditions required for societies to preserve human discretion, role accountability, record continuity, authority-condition boundaries, time-history references, economic reference objects, domain design references, and long-term preservation across heterogeneous AI and AGI environments. The framework does not propose a political authority, legal system, execution platform, public-administration engine, payment rail, evidence-confirmation system, cloud service, model provider, or hardware control layer. Instead, it develops an overarching framework for keeping records, outputs, roles, candidate actions, public references, institutional transfers, and preservation contexts structurally legible when generated materials circulate across providers, institutions, media, networks, local reference hardware, documents, economic environments, design domains, and physical-digital systems. The proposed framework synthesizes coordinate-based document and media reference, output-reference boundaries, human-discretion preservation, role-referenced accountability, post-cloud reference continuity, multi-layer cross verification, generated-output governance, time-history and seal references, authority-condition boundaries, consent and order candidate layers, provider-independent structural reference layers, public institutional reference infrastructures, edge reference nodes, local reference hardware, traceable document states, economic reference objects, domain design reference infrastructures, and propagation-preservation boundaries. Its central proposition is that AI and AGI societies require a non-substitutive reference infrastructure that can preserve continuity without converting reference into authority, preservation into proof, candidate language into action, economic reference into settlement, design reference into construction, public record circulation into public decision, or technical capability into human responsibility. This working paper is Paper 22 of the AGI Structural Alignment Series.

title: The Am That Remains: A Critique of Descartes and a Metaphysics of the Soul
abstract: This essay reexamines René Descartes’ famous cogito (“I think, therefore I am”) by arguing that thinking reveals not the ground of being, but only the activity of temporal consciousness. Drawing on Augustine of Hippo, Thomas Aquinas, and contemplative theology, the paper develops a metaphysical account in which sensation, passion, and discursive thought belong to embodied temporal life, while the soul’s deeper mode is direct apprehension of reality. Death is interpreted not as the extinction of selfhood, but as the removal of cognitive interference through which the soul knows without mediation. The essay proposes an inversion of the Cartesian formula: not I think, therefore I am, but I think because I am.

title: English Article System Errors among Saudi Arab EFL Learners: A Case of the Preparatory Year English Program Learners of King Saud University
abstract: The present study aimed to identify and categorize the errors made by Arabic speaking EFL learners in their use of the English Article System. In addition, it sought to attribute these article errors to their possible sources in an attempt to postulate whether L1 Arabic or L2 English played a key role in learners’ article misuse. To this end, 50 Saudi male EFL learners were subject to an MCQ test, and 5 teachers were interviewed. Surface Structure Taxonomy (SST) of errors was used to classify errors in three major categories, namely omission, addition, and substitution. These major categories were further classified, according to error sources, into two error types, namely interlingual errors and intralingual errors. The study revealed that while Saudi learners made errors in all categories, addition errors were the most frequent. Further, substitution was the second frequent while omission errors showed to be the least frequent type of errors. Analysis of test results and interviewed teachers’ responses showed that most of article errors could be attributed to L1 interference. In many areas, the Arabic Article System was negatively transferred into English where learners seemed to resort to their mother tongue to decide on the appropriateness of using the article in question. However, L2 English, in other cases, was the source of errors. Ignorance or incomplete application of the rule brought learners to commit intralingual errors as well. The results were discussed, and the implications were made.

title: Women, Climate Crisis, And Sustainable Futures: An Ecofeminist Reading of Barbara Kingsolver's Flight Behavior and Octavia E. Butler's Parable Of The Sower
abstract: Abstract Contemporary American literature increasingly responds to the ecological crises generated by climate change, environmental degradation, resource depletion, social inequality, and unsustainable human practices. Barbara Kingsolver’s Flight Behavior (2012) and Octavia E. Butler’s Parable of the Sower (1993) offer powerful literary representations of societies confronting environmental instability and its social consequences. Although the novels differ significantly in genre, historical context, and narrative form, both place women at the centre of ecological and social transformation. This paper examines the representation of women, nature, climate crisis, environmental justice, and sustainable futures in the two novels through an ecofeminist framework. It focuses particularly on Dellarobia Turnbow in Flight Behavior and Lauren Olamina in Parable of the Sower, arguing that their experiences reveal the interconnectedness of environmental exploitation, patriarchal structures, economic inequality, and social vulnerability. In Kingsolver’s novel, the unexpected arrival of monarch butterflies in rural Appalachia becomes a visible manifestation of climate disruption and a catalyst for Dellarobia’s intellectual and personal awakening. In Butler’s dystopian narrative, climate change, drought, water scarcity, violence, economic collapse, and displacement create a world in which Lauren must develop new forms of survival and community. The paper further argues that both novels move beyond representations of ecological catastrophe by imagining possibilities for resilience, ecological consciousness, collective responsibility, and sustainable futures. Their concerns correspond particularly with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including gender equality, reduced inequalities, sustainable communities, responsible consumption, and climate action. Through a comparative ecofeminist reading, this study demonstrates that contemporary American literature can function as an important cultural space for interrogating environmental injustice and imagining alternative relationships between women, society, and the natural world.
