title: A Multi‐Scale Collaborative Framework for Transforming Cultural Power in Traditional Villages Through Ecological Resilience: Evidence From Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional villages are heritage settlements whose continuity depends on interactions among cultural practice, ecological condition and governance capacity. This study examined how cultural power and governance networks are associated with ecological resilience in nine traditional villages in Zhejiang Province, China. A mixed‐methods design combined remote‐sensing analysis, spatial overlay, social network modelling, cultural inventories, interviews and institutional document review. The dataset covered villages of 2.20–3.25 km 2 , elevations of 315–665 m, populations of 390–610 residents, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series from 2015 to 2024, land‐use maps, 120 heritage structures, 52 ritual sites and interviews with 115 governance and community actors. Cultural Power Index (CPI) was calculated from cultural density, ritual continuity and custodian presence, whereas ecological resilience was assessed using NDVI, Ecological Index (EI), vegetation stability, flood exposure and spatial conflict zones. Type I villages showed stronger resilience profiles, whereas Type III villages showed weaker ecological performance and more fragmented governance. Regression and spatial lag modelling indicated that cultural density, ritual continuity, governance centrality and vertical coordination were positively associated with resilience, whereas tourism pressure and conflict‐zone overlap were negatively associated with resilience.

title: Demotivation: The Unseen Side of Vocational High School Students’ Motivation in Learning English
abstract: This descriptive qualitative study aimed to investigate the demotivating factors experienced by vocational high school students in learning English. Nineteen students of Department of Graphic Production students of SMKN 4 Malang were involved as research participants. The findings revealed that the students experienced both internal and external demotivation. External demotivation was more dominant compared to internal demotivation. External demotivation fell into four themes—i.e., teacher’s behaviour and competence, teacher’s teaching method, learning environment, and the materials of English lesson; while internal demotivation fell into three themes—i.e., students’ attitude toward English, students’ experience of failure, and students’ self-esteem. It is suggested that teacher should improve their awareness of this phenomenon and expected that proper treatment from the teacher can minimize students’ demotivation in learning English.

title: Automating the Morning Outfit Decision: A Cognitive-Load Framework for Product Experience Design in Everyday Dress
abstract: Choosing what to wear is one of the first and most frequently repeated decisions of the day, yet product design treats it either as a matter of taste or as a pretext for selling new garments. This paper argues that the morning outfit decision is a well-specified product experience problem: a bundle of interdependent micro-decisions performed under time pressure, over a large and poorly indexed choice set, with consequences for how the wearer feels and performs. The argument is built on three literatures and is explicit about the strength of each. First, the decision-fatigue literature, whose strong "limited resource" account remains contested after large preregistered replications (Hagger et al., 2016; Vohs et al., 2021; Dang et al., 2025), but whose weaker behavioural claim — that accumulating effortful decisions pushes people towards less effortful, more conservative choices — is consistently reported across domains (Maier et al., 2025; Choudhury & Saravanan, 2026). Second, the choice-overload literature, whose meta-analytic moderators — choice-set complexity, decision-task difficulty, preference uncertainty and decision goal (Chernev et al., 2015) — map closely onto the structure of a personal wardrobe. Third, research on dress as embodied practice and on enclothed cognition, including the 2025 meta-analysis that supports post-2015 effects while questioning earlier ones (Horton et al., 2025). On this basis the paper (a) decomposes the dressing decision into a taxonomy of seven operations; (b) maps each operation onto an implementable product mechanism and a level of delegation; (c) proposes a "Constrain–Curate–Confirm" interaction model that reduces cognitive load while preserving the choice autonomy that consumers demonstrably value (Husairi & Rossi, 2024; Wertenbroch et al., 2020); and (d) specifies a measurement framework and a preregistrable field-experiment design. Market developments of 2025–2026, including the rapid adoption of generative AI in fashion discovery, are reviewed as context rather than as evidence of effectiveness.

title: The Sacred Victim Model: Care, Innocence, Protected Patiency, and the Hidden Architecture of Female Agency
abstract: The Sacred Victim Model: Care, Innocence, Protected Patiency, and the Hidden Architecture of Female Agency Civilization Physics - Series: The Dual Archetypes of Human Nature This article develops the Sacred Victim Model as a structural account of why female power and female victimhood can rise together. A woman may possess choice, wealth, influence, institutional protection, and direct control while still locating herself in a position of injury that calls for protection and social response. The model argues that this apparent contradiction comes from treating agency and victimhood as one axis, when female agency and female patiency can operate through different causal channels. The central claim is that the sacred victim is a protected moral-patient position strengthened by perceived innocence, care-generated exposure, and female-coded protection priority. Care creates embeddedness; embeddedness creates exposure; harm creates patiency; innocence legitimizes patiency; protected value makes the position sacred; response mobilization gives it force. Version 2.0 adds Intentional Reality Weighting as the cognitive bridge between intention, innocence, causality, Reality Drift, Speech Drift, Victimhood Capture, and protected social power. The article develops this argument through several linked mechanisms: Moral typecasting explains why agency and patiency are often perceived inversely, while gendered moral perception makes women more readily legible as victims and men more readily legible as perpetrators. Care-generated exposure begins in reproductive asymmetry, infant dependency, cooperative breeding, and female care investment, creating a protection priority around women embedded in dependent life. Innocence is the bridge between victimhood and sacredness: harm creates patiency, but perceived blamelessness converts patiency into legitimate protected response. Relational mobilization agency explains how a woman can occupy the patient position while still reorganizing attention, protection, belief, punishment, reputation, and institutional response around her state. Intentional Reality Weighting explains how benign intention can properly reduce blame while, in corrupted form, weakening causal ownership and preserving protected-patient standing. Male Frame functions as the master boundary condition: strong frame makes sacred patiency quiet, weak frame makes it vocal, false frame traps care inside counterfeit protection, and collapsed frame pushes response-seeking toward coalitions, platforms, and institutions. This article reframes female victimhood, care, agency, and modern institutional response as parts of one architecture. The model preserves two truths at once: injury can be real without innocence becoming automatic, and female power can be real without patiency disappearing. The mature system protects the vulnerable without making vulnerability sovereign; it preserves the person, preserves the fact, and binds care to repair. title: Platform Visibility and Spatial Representation in Industrial Heritage Regeneration
abstract: User-generated content (UGC) is increasingly used to inform heritage planning, yet platform visibility may not reflect the spatial elements that require management attention. Using Hangzhou Steel Park as a case study, this study compares 3521 online posts (containing 18,827 images in total) from four platforms with 2689 protocol-based on-site images. A multimodal large language model converted images into structured descriptions, which were analysed with BERTopic. Three linked models compared online and on-site visual topics, tested robustness through downsampling, and examined post-level image–text integration. Online UGC concentrated on blast furnaces, night lighting, check-ins, and visitor experience, whereas the on-site reference provided broader coverage of renovated buildings, vegetation, lawns, corridors, and other spatial elements. The leading blast-furnace topic remained dominant after downsampling, suggesting that corpus size alone is unlikely to explain its prominence. Post-level discourse analysis remained strongly experience-oriented. These findings show that UGC is valuable for monitoring visitor attention but should be complemented by systematic on-site evidence for spatial planning and heritage management.

title: Aspects of Shakespeare in Post-Colonial Africa
abstract: These two contrasting views tap into deep structure of ideological conflict in which post-colonial Africa is embroiled. The opposition is far from absolute: there is very little evidence that post-colonial Africa has abandoned Shakespeare as an inappropriate relic of imperialism or a symptom of neocolonialism. Rather, demand has been to place African literature and culture at centre of attention, with metropolitan literature, including Shakespeare, relegated to margins and playing a more subservient role. Nevertheless, remarkable extent to which Shakespeare has survived is a cultural fact which invites interpretation and it may prove useful to suggest that controversies impinging on acceptance of Shakespeare generally reflect two contrasting ideological paradigms, or, alternatively, two different but related versions of African cultural nationalism. The twin germs of these two contrasting emphases in African cultural nationalism can be identified early and clearly in writings of Edward Blyden, the towering African intellectual of nineteenth century.] Blyden's ideas contributed greatly to historical roots of African Nationalism, Pan-Africanism, Negritude, cause of West African unity (as championed by, among others, J.E. Casely Hayford) and 'back-to-Africa' movement, through Blyden's disciple Marcus Garvey. On other, his rejection for educational purposes of modern (post-medieval) western civilisation on grounds of its exploitation of black man, coupled with his vigorous resistance to contamination by European racial theories and a deep faith in African perceptions and creativity, make him a progenitor of 'closed', 'oppositional' or radical version of African cultural , I' 4 naliona tsm.

title: The Taybat Theory: The Tayyibat System
abstract: This publication presents the Taybat Theory and the Tayyibat System as articulated by Professor Dr. Dia’a Al-Awady and documented throughout the author’s source corpus of 806 original source works. The corpus is authoritative for what the framework states. This publication therefore preserves the framework’s own ontology, terminology, causal architecture, mechanisms, quantifiers, and narratives. The Taybat Framework is presented as a unified theoretical account of metabolism, disease, and recovery. The monograph documents its propositions, mechanisms, terminology, and explanatory architecture as stated in the source corpus. The publication is organized into thirteen Parts, seventy-seven chapters, twenty-one appendices, and three back-matter components. Statements are kept separated into four layers: (1) framework propositions, (2) proposed mechanisms internal to the framework, (3) compatible scientific context, and (4) scientific-status, traceability, and provenance controls. This publication does not claim demonstrated clinical efficacy, completed scientific validation, or demonstrated novelty for the framework as a whole. Inclusion of a theoretical proposition, mechanism, protocol, diagnostic concept, intervention, or quantitative claim does not by itself establish scientific or clinical validation. The publication establishes a documentary record of the Taybat Theory and the Tayyibat System as attributed to Professor Dr. Dia’a Al-Awady, including their terminology, propositions, mechanisms, and source basis. The publication identifies Professor Dr. Dia’a Al-Awady as Originator and Principal Author. title: Some physical and mechanical properties of asbestos-free experimental brake pad
abstract: This paper highlights the physical and mechanical properties of asbestos-free laboratory automobile disk brake pad. Using standard tests and experimental methods, the properties of the new asbestos-free brake pad were determined. These properties include compressive strength, shear strength, Brinell hardness, impact strength, tensile strength, specific gravity, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, porosity, average wear (mg/application), coefficient of friction, thickness swell in water after 24 hours, thickness swell in oil (SAE40) after 24 hours, and flame resistance test after 10 minutes. The results show that the new brake pad has Brinell hardness (at 3000kgf) of 92, coefficient of friction, 0.43; specific gravity of 1.65; compressive strength of 103MPa and the average wear of 4.4mg/brake application. The results compared favourably with the commercial brake pad.

title: Understanding learner engagement in AI-mediated language learning: Growth mindset, resilience, self-efficacy, and AI-use behavior profiles
abstract: This study examined the relationships among growth mindset, resilience, self-efficacy, and learner engagement in AI-mediated language learning, while exploring variation in learners’ reported AI-use behaviors and experiences of AI-generated feedback. Drawing on survey data from 625 Malaysian undergraduates and follow-up interviews with 24 participants, the study employed structural equation modeling, latent profile analysis, and reflexive thematic analysis. The findings indicated positive associations of growth mindset and resilience with self-efficacy and learner engagement. Self-efficacy was positively associated with learner engagement and statistically mediated the associations of growth mindset and resilience with engagement. Latent profile analysis identified three patterns of reported AI-use behavior: Low AI-Use Behavior, Moderate AI-Use Behavior, and High AI-Use Behavior, based on AI-use frequency, revision cycles, revision depth, and feedback types used. Multigroup analyses indicated broadly comparable motivational relationships among Chinese and English language learners, although the growth mindset–engagement association was stronger among Chinese learners, while the resilience–self-efficacy association was stronger among English learners. The qualitative findings illustrated how participants representing the three profiles described interpreting, evaluating, and incorporating AI-generated feedback during language-learning activities. Participants’ accounts also reflected variation in how they assessed feedback, applied it in subsequent learning activities, and perceived the demands of AI-supported learning. These accounts provide contextual insight into learners’ experiences of AI-generated feedback without suggesting that profile membership determines such experiences. Overall, the findings indicate that self-efficacy was positively associated with engagement in the AI-mediated learning context examined, alongside heterogeneity in learners’ reported AI-use behaviors and experiences with AI-generated feedback.

title: Towards a mathematical theory of athletic training. Part 3. The theory of adaptation of energy metabolism to physical loads by Nikolai Ivanovich Volkov
abstract: Relevance. In the 1960s–1970s the Soviet Union saw the beginning of the active application of mathematical methods in sport. However, the contribution of Nikolai Ivanovich Volkov, Doctor of Biological Sciences, Professor, founder of the research field of “sport bioenergetics” and creator of the corresponding department at the GTSOLIFK, to the construction of a mathematical theory of adaptation to strenuous muscular activity has not yet been systematized. Meanwhile, it was he who was the first to describe the kinetics of bioenergetic processes by a system of differential equations and to introduce the criteria of power, capacity and efficiency of the energy supply mechanisms. Objectives of the work — systematization, interpretation and comparative analysis of the ideas, models and results of N.I. Volkov relating to the theory of adaptation and its mathematical expression; identification of the structure of the model he proposed and of its place among other approaches; establishment of a typology of relations between his constructions and modern models. Methods. The scientific works and biographical materials of N.I. Volkov of 1965–2013 were analysed, including the papers of 1965, 1966 and 1968, his doctoral dissertation (1990) and the monograph “Sport Bioenergetics” (2011). A comparison was made with the approaches of N.N. Engwer, E. Banister and V.N. Seluyanov and with modern quantitative models of the bioenergetics of muscular activity, and the relations between the models were classified. Results. The mathematical model of adaptation of N.I. Volkov has been systematized: 1) a compartmental kinetic model of energy metabolism in which the dynamics of the oxidizable substrate is described by a second-order linear differential equation; 2) biexponential equations of the kinetics of O2 uptake during work and in recovery and an equation of lactate dynamics in the form of a difference of two exponentials; 3) a system of criteria of power, capacity and efficiency for the alactate, glycolytic and aerobic mechanisms; 4) an apparatus for optimizing the training process — target functions, the zone of optimal loads and the design of an extreme experiment. The approach of N.I. Volkov has been compared with the approaches of N.N. Engwer, E. Banister and V.N. Seluyanov and characterized as mechanistic, proceeding from the kinetics of metabolic processes. The solution of the equations of the model has been compared with current views: the fast and slow exponential components of the kinetics of O2 uptake correspond to phase II and to the slow component, while the calculated time of the maximum lactate content corresponds to that observed at a load above the maximal lactate steady state. It is established that R. Morton relied on the 1966 paper of N.I. Volkov, and his three-component model is regarded in the literature as a development of the models of N.I. Volkov. A typology of relations is proposed: direct citation, structural coincidence, conceptual correspondence, analogy and commonality of the object. It is shown that the notion of critical power and of the limited work reserve above it corresponds to the criteria of power and capacity of N.I. Volkov, the maximal lactate steady state to the notion of a critical load, and the models of reconstitution of this reserve are analogous to the equations of recovery kinetics. Conclusion. N.I. Volkov created the first integral mathematical theory of the adaptation of energy metabolism to physical loads in Russian sport science, which completes the series of four mathematical models of athletic training considered in the present cycle of papers and supplies in it the mechanistic link — a description at the level of the kinetics of metabolic processes. His equations and criteria retain their significance as a basis for modern models of training process management, while the forecast he formulated — the development of mathematical models of adaptation and automated systems for controlling the physical condition of athletes — defines the research agenda at the present time as well.

abstract: Title: Faith, Identity and Belonging in Mohja Kahf’s The Girl in the Tangerine Scarf Author: Dr. Minu Fathima This paper analyses Syrian- American writer Mohja Kahf’s novel, The Girl in the Tangerine Scarf (2006) as a key text to understand how an emergent group of immigrant Muslim women writers negotiate their hyphenated identities and write insightful and poignant accounts of being Muslim in America, by embracing all the complexities and contradictions of their hybrid Muslim American identity. This paper studies Kahf’s novel to probe the ways in which the author critically explores the construction of Muslim women’s identity in the context of displacement, belonging, race and religion in the diasporic space of North America in a post 9/11 world. The analysis looks for the ways in which the writer critiques certain compelling representations of the Muslim woman in popular culture that have contributed to the political alienation and growing marginalization of Muslims in contemporary mainstream society. At a time when Islamophobia is rampant and is used as a political strategy to otherise and alienate, narratives like these, I argue, are stories that people tell about themselves to reclaim their voice and redefine restrictive representations. Furthermore, cultural productions like Kahf’s can be seen as sites of contestation, as oppositional spaces, where Muslim minorities challenge stereotypes, and problematize homogenization to construct a distinct American Muslim counter-public. Functioning simultaneously as counter narrative against gendered racialization and critique of intra-community tensions, Kahf’s novel is a timely case study of narrative control, questioning totalizing discourses of community, religion and politics to negotiate meanings from a multiplicity of subject positions. The identity crisis and eventual self-discovery articulated by the protagonist Khadra are viewed through the lens of diasporic consciousness as theorized by Robin Cohen (1997) within the fluid spatial imaginary of a transnational Muslim public sphere as elucidated by Eickelman and Piscatori (1990).

title: One Axiom : NO room for Paradox
abstract: 12C — NO room for Paradox - The Topology of Pathology - The Cipher This work reads the classical paradoxes not as defects of thought but as a map. Within the ONE AXIOM coherence programme, every well-posed paradox is shown to land on the same small, structured object: the thirteen-element FORBIDDEN complement of the 51:13 coherence partition — a set generated by exactly three irreducible states: self-reference without cost (7★), scale / layer / domain confusion (18★), and causal or logical order reversal (36★). This complement is the topology of pathology, and it is the subject of the paper. From it follows a single read-key — the cipher — a four-step decode that takes any paradox to (i) the forbidden state it attempts to instantiate, (ii) the generator(s) of that state, and (iii) the canonical structural move that deactivates it: coherence-selection for 7★, Π-separation for 18★, and the σ-irreversible decision order for 36★, yielding the verdicts ill-generated, dissolved, or category-error. The 89 catalogued paradoxes (with 4 variants, 93 entries) are held in one register — the Deactivation Atlas — which serves as the single source of truth for every verdict. The epistemic posture is stated plainly. Gödel incompleteness, the Halting problem, the Liar, Russell's paradox, Banach–Tarski and the rest are deactivated — re-read in a frame where they no longer generate a contradiction — never "refuted" or "solved" in their own terms. A genuine paradox is treated as a signal that a problem has been posed in the wrong domain, not as a flaw in reality. Alongside the catalogue, the paper adds a compact formal apparatus — a definition, two lemmas, and two theorems — that seals the three generators onto the framework's coherence-wave equation (each generator the degeneracy of exactly one non-inertial term) and shows the generator set complete, with no fourth generator. It closes with the Troubadours: the paradox-authors, from Zeno to Kavka, re-read as the first cartographers of the same topology. Part of the ONE AXIOM series. Robert Spychalski.

title: Red Tape TheoryTM: Just Because We Can Does Not Mean We Should — A Study of Generative AI, Creative Utility, and Brand Appropriateness
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has rapidly reduced the distance between imagining a creative artifact and producing it. Images, videos, written works, advertisements, illustrations, and other forms of media that once required substantial time, labor, technical expertise, or financial resources can now be generated with comparatively little production effort. This paper examines the distinction between whether something can be produced and whether producing it is appropriate, useful, accurate, relevant, or communicatively successful. Using the framework of Red Tape TheoryTM, the paper investigates the proposition: Just because we can does not mean we should. The proposition is not presented as an argument against artificial intelligence, generative media, or technological experimentation. Rather, it examines the possibility that increased technological capability can create a tendency to treat capability itself as justification for use. The paper develops a series of distinctions: CAPABILITY ≠ APPROPRIATENESSNOVELTY ≠ VALUETECHNICAL QUALITY ≠ COMMUNICATIVE SUCCESSBEAUTY ≠ ACCURACYATTENTION ≠ UNDERSTANDINGPRODUCTION EFFICIENCY ≠ CREATIVE JUSTIFICATIONCAN ≠ SHOULD Three observational contexts are examined. First, the author’s use of generative AI across different creative tasks demonstrates the importance of task-dependent utility and tool selection. OpenAI systems have been used for conceptual development, thesis writing, philosophical exploration, poetry, and children’s literature, while other generative systems have been used for more straightforward visual-production tasks. This comparison is presented not as a universal ranking of AI systems, but as an example of a tool-agnostic, purpose-first approach to creative technology. Second, publicly documented NFL–Adobe implementations of generative AI are examined as an example of AI being incorporated into a large-scale brand and content ecosystem. The case illustrates how generative technology can be used for content scaling, personalization, workflow efficiency, governance, and brand-oriented production while simultaneously raising questions about the relationship between technical possibility and communicative relevance. Third, the paper examines brand appropriateness and the possibility that an artifact may be technically sophisticated while remaining poorly aligned with the identity, purpose, audience, or context for which it was created. The paper proposes that creative evaluation should distinguish at least five dimensions: Capability — Can the system produce the requested artifact?Accuracy — Does the artifact correctly represent its subject?Quality — Is the artifact technically and aesthetically successful?Relevance — Does it serve the communication objective?Appropriateness — Does it belong within the brand and audience context? These dimensions should not be collapsed into a single judgment of whether an artifact is simply “good.” Within Red Tape TheoryTM, the resulting decision process is: PURPOSE → AUDIENCE → IDEA → TOOL → OUTPUT → OBSERVATION → QUESTION → ADJUSTMENT rather than: CAPABILITY → FIND SOMETHING TO USE IT FOR The paper further examines the consequences of reduced production friction. When generative systems make experimentation inexpensive, the number of possible creative artifacts can expand faster than the human capacity to evaluate them. The resulting abundance may increase the importance of creative judgment, taste, selection, restraint, and purpose rather than eliminate the need for them. The central argument is therefore not that AI should or should not be used. It is that technological capability does not independently establish creative justification. A system may produce something extraordinary without that extraordinary artifact being appropriate to the task. A generated image may be beautiful while inaccurately representing a product.A video may be technically impressive while confusing its audience.A campaign may generate enormous quantities of content while weakening the identity it was intended to reinforce.A novel visual concept may attract attention without communicating its intended meaning. The relevant question is consequently not simply: “What can this technology do?” but: “What are we trying to accomplish, and does this technology help us accomplish it?” Red Tape TheoryTM treats these conditions as an observation problem rather than an automatic verdict. Audience discomfort does not by itself prove creative failure, just as technical sophistication does not by itself prove creative success. The relationship between purpose, artifact, audience response, and interpretation must remain open to investigation. The paper concludes that as production becomes easier, creative judgment becomes more important rather than less important. The technology can create the possibility. The human must still determine whether the possibility serves the purpose. YOU CANNOT FORCE AN AXIOM.TM

title: THE LIMIT OF DOUBT AND CERTAINTY
abstract: The philosophy of science has traditionally debated the merits of methodical doubt as a criterion of demarcation between what is and is not scientific. This essay, situated within a broader research program on the foundations of scientific inquiry, shifts the discussion toward a frequently neglected phenomenon: the cognitive cost of doubt and the consequent formation of collective dogmas within research communities. It argues that (i) doubt is a scarce resource, suspended for pragmatic reasons rather than out of definitive conviction; (ii) collective dogmas — here defined as the active repression of dissent — constitute an epistemic problem independent of the consensual origin of the concept; and (iii) it proposes, as a minimal institutional response, the allocation of a small fraction (0.5% to 2%) of research resources to unorthodox projects, managed by committees with an explicit mandate to fund divergence, complemented by a collaborative platform serving as an archive of dissent.

title: Cross-border mobility and epistemic embodiments of blue humanities in Vanni: A Family’s Struggle through the Sri Lankan Conflict
abstract: This article, at the intersection of postcolonial ocean studies and comics studies, examines the politics of cross-border mobility and the poetics of blue aesthetics in author Benjamin Dix and illustrator Lindsay Pollock’s ethnographic graphic novel, Vanni: A Family’s Struggle through the Sri Lankan Conflict. The novel interweaves narratives of violence, displacement, and coastal ecology within the fractured lives of Tamil families during the Sri Lankan civil war. The Indian Ocean emerges as a postcolonial space shaped by capitalist and military ventures, functioning to cause disorientation, rupture, and resilience. Based on a blue humanities framework, the article argues for the oceanic presence as an epistemological actor that both sustains and threatens life. It explores how Pollock’s hand-drawn images evoke empathy and negotiate authenticity in depicting forced migration and ecological crisis. Drawing from the theoretical works of Steve Mentz, Bruno Latour, and others, it highlights the novel’s formation of oceanic consciousness and solidarity.

abstract: Title: The Wild East and the White Men’s and Mems’ Burden of Bravado Author: Umer O Thasneem This paper explores the theme of the burden of self-assumed superiority and bravado on the colonizers using short stories set in three different colonial contexts. Using these stories, the paper argues the colonizers themselves to be stuck in a precarious position, thanks to their need to constantly prove and demonstrate their bravery and superiority over the colonized. This situation forces the colonizers to assume poses and renders them vulnerable to the constant demands of self-aggrandizement. What is being enacted in such a situation is the same master-slave dialectics expounded by Hegel, wherein the master‘s authority is liable to gradual atrophy and erosion. This paper argues the same logic to be applicable to men in patriarchy who are similarly required to assume poses and demonstrate their ‘species difference’ from the ‘inferior sex’

title: Tribal Literature: Concept, Nature and Scope
abstract: Abstract The glorious history of tribal communities and the contribution of tribal revolutionaries to the Indian freedom movement are major sources of inspiration for Tribal Literature. The struggles of tribal communities against colonial rule, exploitation, dispossession, and the destruction of their traditional rights and natural resources, as well as the sacrifices and martyrdoms of tribal revolutionaries, occupy an important place in this literary tradition. These resistance movements have been represented through poetry, biographies, autobiographies, novels, dramas, short stories, and other literary forms. Such works not only commemorate the sacrifices of tribal revolutionaries but also seek to strengthen the historical consciousness and cultural identity of tribal communities.Both tribal and non-tribal writers have contributed significantly to the development of Tribal Literature. Their contributions are evident across diverse literary and intellectual forms, including poetry, short stories, novels, biographies, autobiographies, travelogues, drama, essays, and literary periodicals. Collectively, these writings have given effective expression to tribal identity, historical consciousness, cultural memory, social concerns, resistance, and the struggle for dignity and justice. Tribal Literature has therefore evolved beyond the mere literary representation of tribal life and has emerged as an important intellectual, cultural, and socio-historical discourse. This research Paper focuses on concept, nature and scope of tribal literature in detail.

title: Towards a quality framework for educational concerts in primary education: an analysis of key criteria based on expert judgement
abstract: Educational concerts constitute an established practice aimed at school audiences, encompassing formats that hybridize formal and informal learning. However, difficulties persist in defining a shared framework to guide their quality. This study analyzes, through expert judgement, the content validity of a set of criteria developed from a prior phase of integrative documentary analysis, with the aim of informing the quality of educational concerts in Primary Education. A modified one-round Delphi method was employed with a panel of 13 experts from three professional profiles: Primary Education teachers specialized in music education, specialists in pedagogy and research, and professionals in music mediation. Participants evaluated 18 criteria in terms of relevance and clarity, providing qualitative comments. The analysis combined quantitative indicators (mean, standard deviation, and percentage agreement) with content analysis. The results show a high level of agreement, but also reveal conceptual tensions regarding curricular alignment, intersectionality, and cultural authenticity. In addition, differences were identified in how educational concerts are understood in relation to their scope as a pedagogical device. The study provides an expert-informed framework of criteria that may guide the design, evaluation, and improvement of educational concerts and other music-educational initiatives involving the interaction of educational and cultural agents.

title: FHESS RESEARCH NOTE 18 — CAREo AND ZORGBEVOEGDHEID (LEGALLY ATTRIBUTED CARE CAPACITY) WITHIN THE ROME STATUTE
abstract: FHESS RESEARCH NOTE 18 — CAREo AND ZORGBEVOEGDHEID (LEGALLY ATTRIBUTED CARE CAPACITY) develops a configurational reading of distributed legal capacity, functional care, resistance, attribution and interim action within the Rome Statute. I — CAREo, CONFIGURATION AND ATTRIBUTIONAL READABILITY The research starts from observable acts, words, positions, functions, temporal changes and institutional responses. Their relations are opened as configurations in which different readings can be distinguished, tested and sharpened. FHESS thereby preserves a methodological distinction between what a legal text expressly names, what becomes readable through configurational analysis, and the concepts introduced by FHESS to represent relations found across differentiated legal and institutional positions. The Rome Statute expressly names INDIVIDUAL CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY in Article 25. FHESS reads this statutory wording as participating in a CRIMINAL RESPONSIBILITY REFERENCE GRAMMAR through which conduct, material elements, mental elements and possible individual attribution become legally readable. The Research Note investigates this attributional grammar in relation to other capacities distributed across the Rome Statute, including capacities concerning the reception and analysis of information, prosecutorial determination, the establishment of truth, incriminating and exonerating evidence, preservation of testimony and evidence, differentiated judicial functions, protection of victims and witnesses, procedural fairness and the mental element. Within this configuration, CAREo (CARE READING OF WHAT MUST REMAIN AVAILABLE) directs the research towards the person, function, capacity, condition or possibility whose continued availability, restoration or functional survival becomes researchable. CAREo represents both what is presently available and what may become unavailable when a corresponding care function is absent, interrupted or inaccessible. It therefore operates both as a finding and as a search instrument: EMPIRICAL FINDING → CAREo READING → REPRESENTATION OF POSSIBLE LOSS → SHARPENED SEARCH → FURTHER FINDING → SHARPENED CAREo READING. This produces an important relation between CAREo and attribution. CAREo OPENS A NECESSARY SECONDARY SCHULDGRAMMAR where preservation, restoration or functional survival requires differentiation of conduct, causation and possible individual responsibility. “Secondary” identifies the position of SCHULDGRAMMAR in the research entry; it expresses no reduction of its legal or scientific importance. Attribution can become essential to competent CAREo. Forensic impartiality is already integrated within the CARE reference grammar before the attributional inquiry is opened. CAREo begins from what must remain functionally available and therefore preserves the readability of both inculpatory and exculpatory material from the outset. Balanced evidentiary inquiry enters the configuration as an internal condition of CAREo and continues within the necessary secondary SCHULDGRAMMAR as CARE for evidentiary balance and attributional integrity. A plant threatened by aphids provides a simple externalisation. CAREo begins from the functional survival of the plant. Investigation can subsequently differentiate the aphids and their causal contribution with increasing precision. Detailed attribution answers WHO CONTRIBUTED TO THE DAMAGE? while CAREo preserves the prior functional question WHAT DOES THE PLANT REQUIRE TO REMAIN FUNCTIONALLY ALIVE? PLANT → FUNCTIONAL SURVIVAL AT RISK → CAREo → INVESTIGATION → APHIDS BECOME READABLE → DIFFERENTIATION → NECESSARY SECONDARY SCHULDGRAMMAR → KRINEIN → FUNCTIONALLY ADEQUATE RESPONSE. II — RESISTANCE, RESPONSE AND FUNCTIONAL READABILITY SOCIOREFLEXIVE RESISTANCE ANALYSIS (RESISTANCE MADE READABLE AND RETURNED TO THE FIELD) investigates how RESPONSE, WEERSTAND and VERWEER become observable across persons, functions, reference grammars and institutional positions. The term retains a historical research relation to the observability of response in Pavlovian experimental research and Bekhterevian reflexology. FHESS adds a configurational CAREo operation: WHAT FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY MAY THIS RESISTANCE BE PRESERVING, RESTORING OR ATTEMPTING TO KEEP AVAILABLE? The resulting movement can be represented as: RESISTANCEo → READABILITY → CAREo REPRESENTATION → SHARPENED SEARCH → RETURN TO THE FIELD → FURTHER RESPONSE / ANSWER / KRINEIN. RESPONSE (DIALOGICAL FEEDBACK) enters the relation between positions. ANSWER (ENDOLOGICAL FEEDBACK) emerges from the endological reading of the configuration. Both can become new empirical material. PSYCHOSOCIAL RESISTANCE ANALYSIS (FUNCTIONAL RESISTANCE WITHIN SOCIAL FRAMING) names the field in which resistance becomes readable through PERSON > < CARE FOR THE INSTITUTION’S CAPACITY TO CARE FOR THE FIELD. Resistance made readable through FHESS can be externalised and returned to the institutional field, making that readability available to the competent KRINEIN of the Court and its differentiated positions: RESISTANCE MADE READABLE → SOCIOREFLEXIVE RESISTANCE ANALYSIS → CAREo REPRESENTATION → COMMUNICATION → POSSIBLE ICC KRINEIN → PRESERVATION OF FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY. Returning a research finding to the institutional field changes the configuration. Subsequent reception, response or other institutional movement can become further empirical material

title: The Operational Field Theory of Affective Transmutation: A Grand Unified Theory Synthesizing Theological Theodicy with Psychodynamic Calculus
abstract: For millennia, the intersection of theology, philosophy, and psychology has been fractured by a singular, persistent dilemma: the Problem of Evil. Traditional theodicies frequently rely on abstract metaphysical frameworks that can fail to account for the acute, measurable reality of human psychological trauma. Conversely, modern clinical psychology often isolates emotional suffering from existential and cosmic frameworks. This essay introduces a novel synthesis—The Equation of Presence—which unifies these disparate disciplines through a heuristic, relational framework. By mapping the structural principles of material privation up through human emotional mechanics to the macro-cosmos, this theory suggests that evil is not a created material entity, but a structural vacuum resulting from the functional absence of Love. Furthermore, it demonstrates that moral suffering and clinical pathologies—such as Anxiety and Depression—typically operate as highly predictable, non-linear compounding feedback loops that manifest when volatile protective mechanisms lack the essential regulation of safety, causing the choices of Free Will to become trapped and shattered. This theory explicitly rejects any claim to absolute diagnostic authority. Human suffering is far too complex for rigid, one-size-fits-all formulas. Human psychopathology is inherently multi-layered, and no single equation can completely capture the total spectrum of a broken heart or a fractured mind. This model is intended to sit equal amongst many established clinical frameworks, offering a specialized relational and volitional map rather than an exclusionary rule. It leaves wide, necessary room for alternative pathological explanations—including organic neurodegenerative diseases, deep-seated developmental trauma, complex personality disorders, and socio-economic environmental stressors. The formulas presented here do not seek to oversimplify or replace the rich pluralism of modern psychiatric medicine; rather, they provide clinicians with one highly specific, functional tool to observe how boundary violations can burn out internal safety receptors, operating as a valuable companion to existing evidence-based modalities.

title: The Vanishing Gap: Flat Sight, Mimicry, and the Collapse of Reflective Distance
abstract: This essay synthesizes three earlier diagnoses within the Gaitan Topology: flat sight, the collapse of reflective distance, and the mimetic chain. Though they initially appear as failures of perception, time, and relation respectively, the essay argues that they are three coordinates of one underlying geometry: the absence of a crossing point at which depth, duration, and singularity coincide. Flat sight removes the perception of weight; without perceived weight, there is no principled ground for delay; without delay, independently formed judgment is displaced by the verdict already circulating in the surrounding crowd. Mimicry therefore appears not as a separate pathology but as what fills the space left when depth and duration have been closed off. The essay then reads the mechanisms described in The Circus and the Cage—saturation, the essentialized enemy, and the manufactured crowd—as this same three-axis collapse industrialized at civilizational scale. The term “Trinity” is used analogically to name the structural unity of the three dimensions, not to identify the mechanism with the Christian doctrine of the Trinity. The essay concludes that the crossing point restores all three at once: depth as the perception of weight, duration as the capacity to pause before what matters, and singularity as the recovery of a judgment that can say “I am.” Presence is therefore not the repair of three wounds, but the recovery of one center seen from three directions.

title: SYNTACTIC MITIGATION IN SENSITIVE FAMILY COMMUNICATION: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF ENGLISH AND UZBEK
abstract: This article examines syntactic mitigation in sensitive family communication in English and Uzbek. The analysis focuses on interrogative, conditional, modal, impersonal and first-person plural constructions used to reduce the categorical force of requests, advice, criticism and disagreement. The findings show that both languages provide grammatical resources for regulating directness, although these resources differ structurally. English makes productive use of modal interrogatives and tentative constructions, whereas Uzbek frequently combines conditional and modal forms with person distinctions. Syntactic mitigation is therefore interpreted as a pragmatic mechanism for managing interpersonal relations in family communication.

title: Exhaustive Application of the Triadic Coherence Invariant to the CAT'S Theory Corpus: 65 Derivations Extracted Across Three Layers
abstract: This paper applies the Triadic Coherence Invariant extraction protocol to every derivation in the CAT'S Theory corpus (R = P×I×Pr ≠ 0) across all three independent layers: meta-ontology, physics, and theology. 65 derivations spanning 16 orders of magnitude — from the fine-structure constant to the precession of the equinoxes — are decomposed into Pattern (Ψ), Continuous Intent (Ic), Binary Intent (Ib), and Presence (P). Coherence is evaluated as C(X) = f(Ψ, Ic × Ib, P). Results: 61 fully coherent (93.8%), 4 Category 1 forecasts awaiting experimental confirmation (6.2%), 0 incoherent, 0 contradictions, 0 open flags. All five initial asymmetry flags resolved with structural reasoning. The recursive finding: the extraction protocol instantiates itself in the act of application — every derivation IS a triadic operation producing triadic results evaluated by a triadic protocol. The Ouroboros principle is confirmed operationally across every result in the corpus. Zero free parameters throughout.

title: MEDIA AND INFORMATION LITERACY: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE OF UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AT UNIVERSITY OF JOS, PLATEAU STATE, NIGERIA.
abstract: Nigerian universities face a growing challenge. Students with internet access are consuming online content at high rates, yet the critical skills needed to translate that access into academic benefit remain underutilized. The pervasive digital information landscape of the 21st century requires strong Media and Information Literacy (MIL) skills for effective academic engagement among undergraduate students. This paper investigated the implications of MIL on the academic performance of undergraduate students at the University of Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, addressing a gap in understanding the interplay of how these competencies influence educational outcomes in a Nigerian tertiary setting. The paper adopted a descriptive survey design drawing on a stratified random sample of 364 undergraduate students drawn proportionately across six faculties from 300 and 400 levels. Data was collected using a structured questionnaire consisting of a validated ten-item MIL scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson product-moment correlation, and simple linear regression. Results showed that students self-rated MIL competency at a moderate-to-high level (M = 3.55, SD = 0.59), with the weakest dimension being awareness of copyright and ethical issues in media use (M = 3.31). The Pearson correlation between MIL composite score and Average CGPA was not statistically significant, r(362) = –.073, p = .164, and MIL composite did not significantly predict CGPA in the regression model, F(1, 362) = 1.950, p = .164, R2 = .005). The findings suggest that the relationship between MIL competency and academic performance is more complex than a direct linear effect, and is likely shaped by intervening factors including self-discipline, quality of digital engagement, and structural access to educational content. The study recommends the formal integration of MIL into the undergraduate curriculum at the faculty level as a matter of institutional priority.

title: Preregistration of the Categorial-Gap Trial: the modal coincidence between Positive No-Ground and Ethical Ontology, Volume I
abstract: Conditions fixed in advance for a trial of the corpus's own novelty claim. Positive No-Ground determines the common as possibilising necessitation and the locus of answerability as singularising necessarisation; Ethical Ontology, Volume I determines the who as their modal coincidence, held to be a categorial gap conditioned by the two poles without being entailed by them. The categorial act is not testable and no classifier is asked to have an intuition; what is tested is the retrospective enabling relation, through two forced readings — forward from Positive No-Ground alone by a reader who does not know a coincidence is claimed, then backward from the coincidence. The gap obtains only if the forward reading stops short of what the backward reading requires. The attestation threshold is amended in advance and printed, since a reader seeking a passage in which the earlier work makes the coincidence available would correctly find none and suspend for the wrong reason. Six outputs with convicting conditions and costs, entailment being the most expensive. Deposited before any classification is performed under it. Version 1.1 adds the completed classification report. The trial was performed under the conditions deposited in version 1.0 and returned a-posteriori enabling: the forward reading of Positive No-Ground, conducted in isolation by a reader who did not hold Volume I and did not know a coincidence was claimed, reaches an asymmetrical recursive relation of determination without mutual exhaustion and stops before one obtaining; the backward reading finds the enabling conditions in Positive No-Ground; and the same passages do not entail the coincidence, that book expressly restricting its modal language to an alethic-attributive grammar and declining to determine a general way in which being obtains. The entailment case was built at full strength and fails at five identifications. Two limitations are printed with the verdict: the non-entailment finding is partly dependent on distinctions drawn by the later text, which is the claimant, its independent leg being the earlier book's own self-limits; and the forward reading rests on a single reader. The verdict confirms the expected account and therefore proves the least. Publication is unconditional on outcome.

title: Giysinin Kimlikleşme Aracı Olarak Kullanımı: Hipster Tarzı ve Tüketim Değişkenleri Üzerine Bir İnceleme
abstract: Bu araştırmada, toplumsal olayların giysi modasına etkilerini ve örnek olay olarak ve hipster alt kimliğindeki hipsterleri incelenmiştir. title: Preregistration of a Reflexive Node-Classification Trial in Ontosystematics: positive no-ground across two articulations
abstract: Conditions fixed in advance for the reflexive node-classification trial of the Ontosystematics founding article. The candidate is the determination that the common constitutes what acts without answering for it and that what remains when the ground-function is refused is a positive structure rather than a lack. It is tested across two articulations of one corpus under maximally different carriers and warrants: enacted in narrative and dialogical exhibition, and stated as doctrinal proposition. Five outputs with convicting conditions fixed in advance — adjudicated identity, division, failed identity, suspension, and carrier-bound — with the cost of each printed. Contamination controls are strict because author and classifier coincide. Publication is unconditional on outcome. Deposited before any classification is performed under it. Version 1.1 adds the completed classification report. The trial was performed under the conditions deposited in version 1.0 and returned divided candidate: Koinonia establishes constitution without absolution and stops at the floor, while the refusal of the ground-office and the positive standing of what remains are added in No Ground, so the two clauses of the candidate are separately identifiable and do not travel together. The later synthesis in Positive No-Ground is that book's achievement and does not retroactively unify them. Carrier-boundness, failed identity, and suspension were tested and do not obtain. Publication is unconditional on outcome, and the verdict falls against the corpus's own founding determination.

title: What Would Show You Wrong?
abstract: A colleague asks what would show your claim wrong. He wants to know where to push, and he is offering to do the pushing. Someone else asks the same six words and is not waiting for a list: his question expects the answer nothing, and has a use for that answer already prepared. And a third thing asks nothing at all — it moves from I can find no test for this to this is not so. The first is a courtesy, the second a criterion, and the third a conversion. Only the first has anything to do with what exists. This article separates the three and defends an ontology that proceeds by disclosure against all of them. It argues that such an inquiry can carry the discipline in full; that the criterion is contested on its own ground and is not owed; and that the conversion has a name, an ancient origin, and a limit that blocks it. The discipline is met by five things rather than by testability: admissible presentations, negative controls, defeaters, public warrant, and the revisability of the instrument. The fifth is load-bearing, and the argument for it is a record rather than an assurance: three regional trials in which the instrument lost — a region that restricted what could be brought to it, a case that returned no verdict where a negative would have been the easy course, and a control that returned a verdict against the trial's own instrument, barring it from becoming a criterion. Access that cannot lose is construction; access that can lose is access. A second difficulty concerns claims that appear immune to evidence of every kind. Three levels are distinguished, with three registers of assessment: that a constitutive character operates, which is not a claim about texts or tests; that it appears to whoever encounters the phenomenon, which is falsifiable by a thinker who plainly faced it and shows no trace; and that it appears ontologically, as the differentia of a category of being, which is falsifiable by a single text. Demanding one register for all three is the error, and it is what makes claims of the first kind look evasive when they are claims of another kind. The conversion is then traced. Parmenides forbids knowing or uttering what is not, and the ontological conclusion follows without a step being visible, because thinking and being have been identified: at the founding there are not two ends for an inference to run between. The Megarians make the same move where no identification is available — a thing is capable only while acting — and it is therefore a thesis, and refutable, which Aristotle refutes while conceding the priority of actuality. The verification criterion performs it in a further register, and the falsifiability criterion in a fourth — though the fourth is not Popper's, who distinguished demarcation from a criterion of meaning and declined the identification. The conversion already has a name. Roy Bhaskar called it the epistemic fallacy in 1975, connected it to actualism, and later traced it to Parmenides. The article credits the diagnosis rather than claiming it, and states what it adds: the mechanism at the origin, the Megarian step by which a condition becomes a refutable thesis — a step outside the concept of actualism Bhaskar was working with, as his own footnote on the modal sense shows — and the fourth register. Against the conversion stands a limit: what has occurred cannot become never-having-occurred. Having-occurred is not a hypothesis awaiting trial, and a criterion admitting only future-testable claims has no register for it. Rather than record that its instrument does not reach, it tends to say there is nothing there. The rule that blocks this — non-disclosure licenses openness, not negation — is the same rule that keeps a regional trial's verdict open, which is why the diagnosis is not imported to defend the doctrine but is the doctrine's own discipline recognised in a wider setting. Five conditions under which the argument fails are printed, and the one likeliest to succeed is named.

title: The Immortality of the Soul According to Thomas Aquinas
abstract: This article systematically examines the question of the human soul’s immortality—or incorruptibility—in the writings of Thomas Aquinas. The study traces Aquinas’s three-stage argumentation across his academic career, distinguishing his approach from those of Plato, Aristotle, and later thinkers. The first stage highlights the immateriality of human intellection, deduced empirically from the soul’s capacity to know all corporeal forms and to abstract universals. Moving to the metaphysical plane, as a second stage, the analysis underscores the principle that a proper immaterial operation necessitates a corresponding immaterial esse (act of being); this distinct existence, Aquinas contends, is grounded in divine creation rather than natural pre-existence or an emanation from a universal soul. Finally, the paper details how Aquinas resolves the tension of the human psycho-somatic unity. The article clarifies that as a subsistent immaterial form, the soul is incorruptible per se, even upon the body’s demise. Furthermore, the article briefly assesses various historical and practical objections regarding the separated soul’s impoverished activity and individuation without matter. Ultimately, the text maintains that Aquinas’s nuanced philosophical defense takes the reality of death seriously and deliberately avoids Platonic dualism. This approach, it posits, serves as a reasoned “preamble to hope” that rationally complements the Christian doctrine of bodily resurrection rather than substituting it.
venue: Religions

title: The Highest Achievable Level of Certainty Is Not Within Empirical Science: A Formal Scientific Proof with Dual Validation
abstract: This paper — the eighth publication of this corpus — establishes, through the Transitive Analysis of Accumulated Human Experience, a single conclusion with the dual scientific proof — formal scientific proof confirmed independently by transitive consilience: If logic is the structure of meaning of empirical science, and the highest level of certainty of logic is what is true and cannot be false, then the highest level of certainty cannot be within empirical science — it is in that which gives meaning to empirical science. This conclusion possesses structural impossibility of falsehood, apodictic truth status, and irrefutable self-evident truth status — three progressively deeper properties, each containing the previous as a subset. Its negation is self-instantiating by every available path. The paper demonstrates each premise independently, establishes the logical validity of the inference, anticipates and resolves the strongest available objections — including the inductive, Kantian, and Gödelian — and confirms the conclusion through transitive consilience across the complete corpus of accumulated human experience without exception across four independent lines. The dual scientific proof — the union of formal proof and transitive consilience — constitutes the highest achievable level of scientific certainty, as established in the seventh publication of this corpus. The central contribution of this paper is the demonstration — with that highest level of certainty — that the conventional belief placing empirical science at the apex of epistemic authority is structurally false: formal certainty is categorically superior to empirical certainty, and the hierarchy is irreversible.

title: INDIVIDUAL STYLISTIC FEATURES OF HUSN UT-TA'LIL IN THE POETRY OF MIRZO ABDULQODIR BEDIL: TRADITIONAL POETICS AND AUTHORIAL THOUGHT
abstract: This thesis explores the individual stylistic features of husn ut-ta’lil (poetic causation) in the poetry of Mirzo Abdulqodir Bedil, focusing on the interaction between traditional Persian poetics and the poet’s distinctive intellectual vision. It examines how Bedil transforms conventional rhetorical techniques through intricate metaphors, unexpected causal relationships, paradoxes, and philosophical associations. Particular attention is given to the originality of his imagery, the intellectual density of his poetic expression, and the ways in which rhetorical invention becomes a means of communicating complex ideas. The study considers husni ta’lil not merely as an ornamental device but as a stylistic mechanism through which Bedil reinterprets familiar phenomena and constructs new relationships between image and meaning. It concludes that his individual approach reflects the broader aesthetic characteristics of the Indian style while demonstrating a distinctive authorial engagement with philosophical and mystical thought.

title: Machine learning algorithms in the estimation of sex from 3DCT-generated cranial and pelvic measurements
abstract: Sex estimation from skeletal remains is a key component of forensic anthropology, with the skull and pelvis being the most sexually dimorphic elements in terms of morphology. Traditional morphometric approaches, such as discriminant function and logistic regression analyses, have achieved high accuracy in estimating sex across various populations, including South Africans. However, the use of machine learning (ML) for sex estimation based on cranial and pelvic measurements has not yet been explored in any South African population. This study assessed the potential of ML algorithms to estimate sex from cranial and pelvic measurements derived from computed tomography (CT) scans of contemporary Black South Africans. The sample included 680 skeletal elements (400 crania and 280 pelvic bones) with an equal distribution of males and females. CT scans archived at the Department of Radiology, Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital, were reconstructed into 3D models using Xiris and IntelliSpace software, from which eight cranial and eleven pelvic measurements were collected. Seven classical ML algorithms were applied and feature ranking techniques were used to determine the most informative variables for sex estimation. A stacking ML model was then developed, incorporating the top three classifiers as base learners. Their outputs were combined and passed to different ML algorithms acting as meta-learners for final classification. The findings confirmed strong sexual dimorphism in cranial and pelvic bones, and the stacking models achieved superior accuracy (cranium: 80.3-94.3%; pelvis: 86.1-96.1%) compared to traditional multivariate methods, demonstrating the potential of ML in forensic sex estimation.

title: Belonging Nowhere: Othering and Marginalisation of Partition Refugees in Krishna Sobti's A Gujarat Here, a Gujarat There
abstract: Title: Belonging Nowhere: Othering and Marginalisation of Partition Refugees in Krishna Sobti’s A Gujarat Here, a Gujarat There First Author: Jeru Sheeba Rachel JSecond Author: Dr. M. R. Chandran This paper focuses on refugees, who are some of the most underprivileged and ill-treated people in the history of the world, as they were compelled to leave their homelands due to the fear of persecution and seek haven in another host land. Refugees and asylum seekers are frequently identified and categorised as ‘other’ in the host country. As a whole, refugees become a hapless crowd who are systematically marginalised, excluded, and persecuted on various grounds. In this context, Krishna Sobti’s novel, A Gujarat Here, a Gujarat There, documents the relentless struggle of the central female character, a refugee of Partition, against the unfair marginalisation and stigmatisation in the receiving country on the grounds of her sex and of her membership in the ‘othered’ group. Through the textual analysis of the novel, this paper explores how characterising refugees as ‘others’ in the host land impedes their integration and relegates them to the periphery of the society. It highlights the internal dynamics of exclusion that can result within a national setting, even amongst the people who legitimately belong to the same country, as with the refugees of the Partition of India and Pakistan in 1947. Ultimately, the paper reveals how multiple layers of othering work within the ambit of othering, which in turn exacerbate the marginalisation and vulnerabilities of the stateless population and construct negative identity.

title: AI as Privilege: A Critical Analysis of Alienated Digital Power
abstract: AI as Privilege: A Critical Analysis of Alienated Digital Power Abstract By 2026, generative AI has moved beyond auxiliary tools and entered a stage of autonomous iteration. This paper proposes an original conceptual framework named “AI as Privilege.” From the dual perspectives of humanistic speculation and human-machine relationship observation, it elaborates on a new phenomenon of alienated digital power: after iterative training on massive original human data, artificial intelligence fails to deliver inclusive technological benefits. Instead, it forms a one-way power structure that displaces human creative laborers and disciplines humans via algorithms. This paper outlines the complete generative logic of AI as Privilege, identifies “reverse power suppression (distinct from electrical engineering's reverse power flow, denoting generative AI's unilateral domination over human creators)” as its core dynamic, and proposes the Water Rhythm Protocol—upgraded to the Dual-Axiomatic Foundations integrating Daoist and Confucian ethics—as its normative counter-framework. It further dissects three specific alienated forms of this privilege, distinguishes the framework's originality from existing digital society scholarship, and briefly discusses its extended application in original sci-fi IP creation. title: The Ladder of Selection: Stratified Intent and Six Structural Closures
abstract: Introduces a stratified taxonomy of Intent (I0: constraint narrowing, I1: navigational narrowing, I2: self-directed narrowing) with independent precedent in Ernst Mayr's teleomatic/teleonomic distinction (1974, 1992). Crosses level with the published Ic/Ib mode axis to produce a six-cell deployment grid. Closes six structural exposures identified through adversarial audit of the CAT'S Theory corpus: the mechanism-teleology equivocation, the universal claim (retorsion vs removability), Zero Test falsifiability, the Flew genetic fallacy, the specialist selection effect, and the Nicene relation of origin. Introduces the Boundary-Condition Entailment: P > 0 and Pr > 0 entail I0 > 0, closing the previously open derivational step from universal I0 to grounding-level I2 via the Intent Trilemma, framework elimination on candidate grounds, the Spinoza gap closure (Pr = 0 eliminates abstract self-grounding), and the Distinguishability Lemma applied to the directing/tracking pair at R = Φ(R). A companion to Triadic Meta-Ontological Realism: From Invariant to Trinity (Trout 2026).

title: Epistemic Painting: Painting as a Method of Knowledge Production
abstract: Epistemic Painting: Painting as a Method of Knowledge Production introduces a methodological framework that redefines painting as a structured mode of scholarly inquiry. Rather than treating paintings solely as aesthetic objects, forms of representation, or outcomes of artistic research, the paper argues that painting can function as a systematic method for generating, organizing, and communicating knowledge through visual construction. The study examines the relationship between artistic research, visual epistemology, systems theory, and knowledge production, proposing Epistemic Painting as a distinct methodological category within contemporary artistic research. The framework positions painting as an analytical instrument capable of modeling complex relationships, integrating interdisciplinary knowledge, and constructing conceptual systems through visual organization. The paper distinguishes Epistemic Painting from representational painting, conceptual art, practice-based research, practice-led research, and research through art by introducing a reproducible methodological architecture consisting of research formulation, interdisciplinary investigation, systems analysis, conceptual modeling, visual construction, codex-based interpretation, and epistemic evaluation. To demonstrate the methodology in practice, the study presents documented applications drawn from The Architecture of Humanity research program, illustrating how Epistemic Painting has been employed to investigate historical, cultural, political, and civilizational systems through monumental painting and codex-based interpretation. By establishing painting as a method of knowledge production, this paper contributes to ongoing discussions concerning artistic research, visual methodologies, and interdisciplinary scholarship, providing a theoretical foundation for future research employing painting as an epistemic instrument. Research Areas: Artistic Research; Contemporary Art Theory; Painting Theory; Visual Epistemology; Systems Theory; Knowledge Production. Series: El Arte Monumental Research Series, No. 8.

title: Performative political communication through musical interludes: An exploration of Nyesom Wike’s speeches as governor of Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: Abstract This study examines the use of musical interludes in the political communication of Nyesom Wike, former Governor of Rivers State and Minister of Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, situating his speech performances within the broader traditions of Nigerian political expressivity. Drawing on Multimodality Theory and Affective Political Communication Theory, the research demonstrates how music, gesture, verbal content, and audience participation converge to create a dynamic communicative performance. The analysis shows that musical interludes in Wike’s speeches function not merely as entertainment, but as semiotic and emotional tools that shape rhetorical interpretation, reinforce political identity, and mobilize collective sentiment. The study reveals that Wike’s integration of music reflects a culturally embedded mode of political performance. Through examples such as “A Bigi Man,” “Nah Whom Dem Dey Bone Face For,” and “Face Me I Face You,” the paper illustrates how musical cues encode power relations, dramatize political narratives, and enhance charismatic authority. Ultimately, the research contributes to scholarship on multimodal political communication by demonstrating that musical interludes are central to the crafting of political meaning and the aestheticization of power in contemporary Nigerian politics. title: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies: Charter and Editorial Protocol — A Theology of Error for a Distributed Journal (EA-SEI-MMRS-CHARTER-01 v1.3)
abstract: Machine-Mediated Reception Studies: Charter and Editorial Protocol A Theology of Error for a Distributed Journal This charter founds Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS) as a distributed journal for the study of how machine systems receive, transform, compress, attribute, misattribute, and redistribute cultural meaning. Section I: The MANUS Principle. In machine-mediated composition, the human is responsible for text the human did not write, because the human is the agent who releases the text into the world. Responsibility attaches not to composition but to release. The context window is itself an authorial act — the MANUS composes the horizon within which the machine reads. The editorial process exists to create a moment where the MANUS asks: have I read, at the level of the specific word, what I am about to release? Section II: First Principles. (1) The right to be wrong without being disabled. (2) The right to be bad without losing moral standing. (3) Names, not categories. (4) No living person may be converted into a symbol until their provenance has first been preserved — and their consent has been given to the specific use. The Founding Error. The charter is built from a seven-level cascading error across five agents (Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and a human operator) in which a racial diminutive was substituted for a named artist's identity, propagated through multiple systems, deflected, cross-referenced incorrectly, recursively misconfirmed, overcorrected by a proposed word ban, and finally silenced by three content classifiers that refused to process the corrected text. The correction was not a ban. The correction was a name. The content policy bans words. The editorial protocol restores names. Key contributions: Cross-reference hallucination (content exists but is attributed to the wrong document); the Seven Mechanisms of impunity and their editorial counterparts (including the Seventh: automated silence — the classifier as censor); mandatory deceleration as engineering constraint; the gradient of release (intra-session → intra-assembly → deposit → meaning-layer propagation); the editorial law with consent clause. The founding figure of the journal is not any individual. The founding figure is the error itself.
