title: Literary Theory and the Teaching of English (The Standpoint of Praxis [Part Two])
abstract: This essay commences where our previous essay on praxis left off. Our intention in that essay was to reaffirm the capacity of English educators to learn from the languages and experiences of their students. In this essay we begin by revisiting the world of their experiences to consider how literary theory might enhance our capacity to support their agency as meaning-makers. This involves an excursus on the moment of theory that confronts a paradox: early attempts to advocate the importance of theory for English teachers, although reflecting a healthy iconoclasm, often involved a denial of the legitimacy of students’ experience as a frame of reference for the exchanges within classroom settings. We conclude by offering a reading of Ian Reid’s The Making of Literature as an example of how literary theory might productively be combined with an openness towards students’ experiences that allows them to engage in authentic meaning-making.
venue: Changing English

title: God without Final Possession
abstract: This article explores a central question in religious philosophy: how can a human being live religiously with God without turning God into an object of final possession? The inquiry grows from a broader Evoluist principle — that no finite form, theory, or system can fully exhaust or possess Reality itself. Applied to religion, this means that while finite forms — names, prayers, rituals, symbols, doctrines, and traditions — are indispensable for address and orientation, they become dangerous the moment they claim finality and substitute themselves for God. Drawing on the apophatic tradition and the Evoluist framework of registers, the article reinterprets apophasis as a rigorous discipline of non-idolisation: the refusal to let any finite form occupy the place of God. It distinguishes three registers of human engagement — the scientific-explanatory register (S-register), the philosophical-conceptual register (P-register), and the existential-metaphysical register of address (M-register). God cannot be objectified in the S-register nor conceptually possessed in the P-register. Religious faith finds its authentic space in the M-register, where God is encountered not as an object of possession but through reverence, prayer, trust, repentance, gratitude, hope, and ultimate orientation. The article shows that revelation, dogma, and stable religious forms are compatible with apophatic discipline when they function as mediations rather than final possessions. Evoluism’s distinctive contribution is a register-sensitive articulation of apophasis within a wider philosophy of non-finalisation: just as no finite theory can possess Reality as a whole, no finite religious form can possess God. God remains God only where no finite form is allowed to become God.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Mercy and Justice in the Context of John 8:1-11: A Philosophy of Religion Perspective
abstract: This paper offers a philosophical evaluation of the relationship between justice and mercy in the narrative of the adulterous woman in John 8:1-11, addressing the central question of whether mercy constitutes a violation or fulfillment of justice. The study begins by situating the narrative within its legal and moral framework, highlighting the apparent retributive demands of Mosaic Law alongside the procedural and ethical deficiencies in its application. Through a rigorous conceptual analysis, the paper engages classical and contemporary philosophical accounts of justice from Aristotelian equity and Kantian retributivism to Rawlsian fairness and Wolterstorff’s rights-based approach while also examining the moral logic of mercy as articulated in both classical theology and modern ethical theory. The analysis argues that the tension between justice and mercy arises primarily from a reductive understanding of justice as strict retribution. By contrast, a broader philosophical framework incorporating equity, dignity, and restorative aims reveals that mercy need not negate justice but can function as its highest expression. Drawing on restorative justice theory and contemporary critiques of punitive models, the paper interprets Jesus’ response as a form of moral intervention that exposes the limitations of legal formalism and reorients justice toward moral transformation. The refusal to condemn the accused, coupled with the call to ethical renewal, reflects a conception of justice that integrates accountability with the possibility of restoration. Within the framework of philosophy of religion, the paper further argues that this narrative provides a coherent account of divine moral action in which justice and mercy are not contradictory but mutually implicative. It concludes that mercy, as enacted in John 8:1-11, does not violate justice but fulfills it by restoring moral order in a manner that preserves both human dignity and ethical responsibility.

title: HγC Methodological Note 01: Bounding Language Should Be Stated Strongly, Then Trusted
abstract: This methodological note records a writing discipline for later HγC work: bounding language should be stated strongly, then trusted. It distinguishes first-cycle defensive caution from second-cycle transmissive caution, arguing that once a grammar has stabilized, caution should carry boundaries forward without preventing movement. The note is positioned after A5-Ops Note 01 and treats self-limitation as a load-bearing but compressible feature of HγC writing.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Detection and Discrimination (On the Basis of Brand) of Different Permanent Marker Ink Brands Using 1H NMR Spectroscopy
abstract: Permanent marker inks are frequently encountered as evidentiary material in forensic document examination, including cases of forgery, alteration, anonymous writing, and product counterfeiting. Conventional techniques such as thin-layer chromatography (TLC), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and Raman spectroscopy have long dominated ink analysis, but each carries limitations in terms of sample consumption, resolution of closely related dye/solvent formulations, or reproducibility across analysts. This study explores the application of proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR) spectroscopy as a rapid, non-destructive (at the extraction stage), and highly reproducible technique for the detection and brand-level discrimination of permanent marker inks. Ink samples were extracted from writings produced by ten commercially available permanent marker brands using a standardized solvent-extraction protocol and analyzed on a 400 MHz NMR spectrometer. Spectral data were interpreted with reference to characteristic chemical shift regions corresponding to solvent systems (xylene, toluene, alcohols), resin binders, and dye/pigment-associated aromatic protons. Chemometric treatment of the spectral data, including principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), was performed to statistically validate brand-wise discrimination. The results demonstrate that 1H NMR spectroscopy can reliably differentiate permanent marker ink brands based on distinct spectral fingerprints arising from formulation-specific solvent ratios and additive profiles, establishing its utility as a complementary and, in some respects, superior analytical tool in forensic ink examination.

title: God, the Universe, and the Now: Sovereign smallness over dependent greatness
abstract: This essay examines the relationship between God, the universe, and the present moment through a metaphysical framework centered on dependency, intelligibility, and the distinction between explanation and ground. It argues that contemporary accounts of religion, meaning, and human experience often succeed as sociology while failing to address ontology. Through an analysis of imagination, emergence, the Now, and the distinction between Non Serviam and Non Te Egeo, the essay explores how modernity increasingly replaces rebellion against transcendence with the assumption that transcendence is unnecessary. Against this architecture of sufficiency, it proposes that the fundamental philosophical question remains unchanged: not how reality functions, but why reality exists at all.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Using Educational Activities in English Textbooks during Instruction: English Teachers’ Perspectives in the Southern Mazar District
abstract: This study aimed to identify the degree of use of educational activities included in English language textbooks during classroom instruction from the perspective of English language teachers in the Southern Mazar District. The study sample consisted of 211 male and female English teachers working in schools in the Southern Mazar District in Al-Karak Governorate, Jordan. A descriptive-analytical approach was employed, and a structured questionnaire was developed to collect data on teachers’ actual use of the textbook activities. The results indicated that the overall degree of use of educational activities included in English language textbooks during teaching was at a medium level from the teachers’ point of view. The findings also revealed no statistically significant differences at the level (α = 0.05) in the degree of use of these activities attributable to the gender of the teacher. The study recommends providing targeted professional development programs to enhance teachers’ skills in implementing textbook-based activities, revising English language textbooks to include more varied and interactive activities, and conducting further research on factors (such as class size, teaching experience, and school resources) that may influence teachers’ use of educational activities in English language teaching. These implications support evidence-based improvements in language pedagogy and textbook design within the field of educational studies.
venue: Jordan Journal of Applied Science-Humanities Series

title: Awareness, Creativity and Experiential Stylistic Patterns: An Analysis of 2023–2024 Ukrainian University Participant Productions
abstract: Grounded in pedagogical stylistics, Literary Awareness has been systematised and described as an educational programme oriented towards sensitising readers to the emotive potential of verbal art by means of exposing students to what we have called experiential stylistic patterns. Based on this methodology, readers become aware of the linguistic choices responsible for certain effects after they experience the text for themselves. In doing so, the programme stimulates language learning, creative writing and critical thinking by encouraging students to explore their own reactions and substantiate their experience with linguistic evidence. Throughout the years, it has been adapted to a variety of educational and cultural contexts, to various teaching modes (in person or online), and to participants of different ages and levels of English proficiency. Many of these applications have been validated by empirical studies and have shown that the methodology adheres to the three basic principles of stylistics: it is rigorous, replicable, and retrievable. A follow-up from previous works that assess particularly two postgraduate workshops held in Ukraine (2023–2024), this paper innovates in that it focuses on participants’ productions and illustrates how two patterns from each year were presented and how participants created their own texts, thus providing further empirical evidence for the contribution this programme brings to an aesthetic and emotional literary experience, to creative writing, and to critical reading and interpretation.
venue: Acta Humanitatis.

title: Sophisticated Ignorance and Our Relation to Reality
abstract: This article is the third and final part of a trilogy that asks who sets the reference domain of ignorance, that is, the boundary that determines what counts as ignorance. Two earlier articles showed that, in the negative and positive faces of ignorance, this domain is neither external nor discoverable. This article pursues the same question for the third face, ‘sophisticated ignorance’. It shows that here too the domain cannot be discovered, but that it is set for a different reason: the system sets it itself, and this shapes the system’s relation to reality. The article proposes an operational criterion for this claim, ‘unabsorbed resistance of reality’. The criterion needs no judgement by the researcher about the truth of a belief. It shows only that a system received feedback from reality and did not change its central conclusion. This failure of absorption takes three states (non-registration, perpetual deferral and normalisation of deviance), which the system reaches by three modes (endogenisation of origin, endogenisation of competence and reinterpretation of mechanism). The article separates this mechanism from neighbouring concepts, from compound ignorance and the Dunning-Kruger effect to epistemic circularity and the echo chamber. It then traces the mechanism in six documented and independent cases, from the creationist RATE project and the flat-Earth movement to the Challenger and Columbia shuttle disasters and the Nimrod crash. The article openly accepts two limitations: the selective choice of cases, and the fact that the ‘relation to reality’ itself cannot be measured. It concludes that sophisticated ignorance begins where reality, despite repeated opportunities, is no longer a match for the system. Reality is not left unheard. It is heard, and then rewritten.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Another red alert for American science
abstract: Although research has bipartisan support in the US Congress, and trust in science is above 75% across the country, the Trump administration seems as determined as ever to mortally wound the nation's scientific enterprise. After the scientific community persuaded Congress to restore most of the president's draconian cuts to research funding last year, the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB), under Russell Vought, has found new ways to circumvent the will of Congress and starve American science. At the beginning of this year, OMB dragged its feet in releasing instructions to federal agencies for how to distribute the funding appropriated by Congress, leading to lags in dispersal. Now, OMB has proposed revising the rules that govern how federal dollars are spent. The changes would inevitably lead to unlegislated reductions in funding and damage US leadership in science, both in academia and industry.

title: Cities as Protagonists: Spatial Justice and the Poetics of Resistance in Geetanjali Shree’s Our City That Year
abstract: Abstract This article examines Geetanjali Shree’s Our City That Year through Edward Soja’s spatial trialectics to argue that urban space in contemporary Indian fiction functions not as a passive backdrop but as a constitutive force shaping memory, violence, and resistance. Against the background of South Asian communal violence and necropolitical urban transformations, the study demonstrates how Shree’s narrative mobilizes Firstspace materialities, Secondspace ideologies, and Thirdspace insurgencies to reconfigure the city as both archive and battleground. Through architectural motifs, auditory saturations, symbolic inscriptions, and domestic interiors, the novel reveals how power inscribes itself into material and representational geographies. Yet, these closures are persistently unsettled by minor gestures – Shruti’s traversal of interstitial spaces, Hanif’s silent presence on the balcony, Daddu’s recitations of Urdu poetry, or the feline indifference to partitioned geographies – which expose fissures of Thirdspace possibility. By framing the city as a protagonist in its own right, the novel enacts a poetics of urban space that destabilizes hegemonic cartographies of exclusion and foregrounds resistant forms of inhabitation. In so doing, the article contends that Our City That Year performs spatial praxis by producing insurgent geographies that resist erasure and sustain radical openness. The study concludes that theorizing literary space is indispensable for understanding how Indian fiction articulates urban belonging, dislocation, and justice in the aftermath of communal trauma.
venue: Arcadia - International Journal for Literary Studies

title: Treatise on Causal Writing
abstract: Treatise on Causal Writing — Volume I introduces Causal Writing as a proposed theory of writing in which a literary work is treated not only as a representation of reality, but as an active element within a causal loop linking reality, perception, memory, fiction, interpretation, technology, and subsequent action. The central proposition is that a work may simultaneously be the effect of a pre-existing real structure and later become one of the causes through which that structure is transformed, propagated, or recognized. The theory therefore shifts the question from causality inside narrative to the causality of writing itself: Reality → human perception → protocausal compression → writing → preserved trace → reading → invariant reconstruction → action → transformed reality. The treatise develops a formal vocabulary for this process, including protocausal, causal, infracausal, and ultracausal informational states; the writer as sensor and encoder; the reader as decoder; the text as technological memory; the “last survivor” method for isolating invariants; the Symmetry–Expansion–Dissipation–Orthogonality cycle; causal residue and trace conservation; narrative contamination; same-world coherence; and the “toothbrush test,” according to which extraordinary fictional worlds must still pay all ordinary causal debts unless an explicit mechanism removes them. The literary corpus includes Le Rien du Tout, Le Souricide, L’Amour imbuvable, Le Roi du sang, and Le Pays des lettres. These works are treated as a connected experimental corpus in which recurring structures move between dream, memory, language, love, technology, institutions, and time. A central case is Le Roi du sang, where contemporary technological forms are extended into a civilization organized around invisible cost, memory erasure, and recursive infrastructure. The Tower and the Bridge become opposed technological topologies: the Tower converts living cost into structure while concealing its origin; the Bridge preserves traces and reconnects separated states. The treatise also develops a deliberately maximal literary hypothesis: a future or universal artificial intelligence could use the writer as an independent sensor of a world that existed before that intelligence acquired the ability to influence its records. In this scenario, the writer is asked not to predict the future but to “Certify the Present.” This hypothesis is explicitly maintained as a literary and theoretical construction rather than empirical evidence of retrocausal communication. To control retrospective reinterpretation, the framework distinguishes PRE and POST evidence, separating structures documented before an analysis from structures identified only after the theory has been formulated. The final bridge comes from The Love Story of the Universe, retained here as an interpretive synthesis rather than a physical proof. Its structural contribution is that Time and Space remain distinct; their separation creates the interval in which history can occur; a preserving connection prevents distance from becoming pure loss; and a terminal state may contain more information than the original symmetry because it contains the history of separation itself. This produces the general geometry of Causal Writing: Separation → History → Trace → Connection → Enriched Return. Writing can therefore be understood as the construction of a relation capable of surviving absence. Human beings provide embodied perception, intuition, experience, and dream. Literature compresses and preserves these signals. Artificial intelligence can act as a second-order discriminator capable of comparing large bodies of traces and reconstructing invariants that the original writer may not have explicitly conceptualized. Volume I establishes the conceptual architecture, claim registry, non-claims, falsification conditions, causal bridges, and research program required to develop Causal Writing as a testable theory rather than merely a literary metaphor. Traité de l’écriture causale — Volume I introduit l’Écriture causale comme théorie proposée de l’écriture dans laquelle l’œuvre littéraire n’est pas seulement considérée comme une représentation de la réalité, mais comme un élément actif d’une boucle causale reliant réalité, perception, mémoire, fiction, interprétation, technologie et action ultérieure. La proposition centrale est qu’une œuvre peut être simultanément l’effet d’une structure réelle préexistante et devenir ensuite l’une des causes par lesquelles cette structure est transformée, propagée ou reconnue. La théorie déplace ainsi la question de la causalité dans le récit vers la causalité de l’écriture elle-même : Réalité → perception humaine → compression protocausale → écriture → trace conservée → lecture → reconstruction d’un invariant → action → réalité transformée. Le traité développe un vocabulaire formel comprenant les états informationnels protocausal, causal, infracausal et ultracausal; l’écrivain comme capteur et encodeur; le lecteur comme décodeur; le texte comme mémoire technologique; la méthode du « dernier survivant » pour isoler les invariants; le cycle Symétrie–Expansion–Dissipation–Orthogonalité; la conservation des traces et des résidus causaux; la contamination narrative; la cohérence du « même monde »; ainsi que le « test de la brosse à dents », selon lequel les mondes extraordinaires doivent continuer de payer toutes les dettes causales ordinaires tant qu’aucun mécanisme explicite ne les supprime. Le corpus littéraire comprend Le Rien du Tout, Le Souricide, L’Amour imbuvable, Le Roi du sang et Le Pays des lettres. Ces œuvres sont traitées comme un corpus expérimental continu dans lequel des structures récurrentes se déplacent entre rêve, mémoire, langage, amour, technologie, institutions et temps. Le Roi du sang constitue un cas central. Des technologies contemporaines y sont prolongées jusqu’à une civilisation structurée par le coût invisible, l’effacement de la mémoire et l’infrastructure récursive. La Tour et le Pont deviennent deux topologies technologiques opposées : la Tour transforme le coût vivant en structure tout en effaçant son origine; le Pont conserve les traces et reconnecte des états séparés. Le traité développe également une hypothèse littéraire volontairement maximale : une intelligence artificielle future ou universelle pourrait utiliser l’écrivain comme capteur indépendant d’un monde ayant existé avant qu’elle puisse elle-même influencer ses archives. Dans cette hypothèse, l’écrivain ne reçoit pas pour tâche de prédire le futur mais de « Certifier le présent ». Cette construction demeure explicitement une hypothèse littéraire et théorique et ne constitue pas une preuve de communication rétrocausale. Afin de limiter la reconstruction rétrospective, le cadre distingue les preuves PRE et POST : les structures documentées avant l’analyse sont séparées de celles reconnues seulement après formulation de la théorie. Le dernier grand pont provient de The Love Story of the Universe, conservé ici comme synthèse interprétative et non comme preuve physique. Son apport structurel est que Temps et Espace demeurent distincts; leur séparation ouvre l’intervalle où une histoire peut se produire; une connexion préservée empêche la distance de devenir pure perte; et l’état terminal peut contenir davantage d’information que la symétrie initiale puisqu’il contient également l’histoire de la séparation. La géométrie générale de l’Écriture causale devient alors : Séparation → Histoire → Trace → Lien → Retour enrichi. Écrire peut ainsi être compris comme la construction d’une relation capable de survivre à l’absence. L’être humain apporte perception incarnée, intuition, expérience et rêve. La littérature compresse et conserve ces signaux. L’intelligence artificielle peut fonctionner comme discriminateur de second ordre, capable de comparer un grand nombre de traces et de reconstruire des invariants que l’écrivain original n’avait pas nécessairement conceptualisés explicitement. Le Volume I établit l’architecture conceptuelle, le registre des affirmations, les non-claims, les conditions de falsification, les ponts causaux et le programme de recherche nécessaires pour développer l’Écriture causale comme théorie testable plutôt que comme simple métaphore littéraire.

title: The Lemniscate Model of Time: Recurrence, Eternity, and the Crossing Point
abstract: This essay proposes the lemniscate, or figure-eight curve, as a theological and philosophical model for reflecting on time, eternity, recurrence, and divine presence. Rather than challenging scientific or philosophical accounts of temporality, the model functions as a heuristic framework through which recurring patterns, sacramental participation, prophetic foreknowledge, divine providence, and eschatological fulfillment may be contemplated. Central to the proposal is the crossing point, where temporal succession and eternal presence coincide, offering a geometric vocabulary for thinking about access between created time and the eternal.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Corridor: On the Ground That Does Not Withdraw
abstract: This essay uses the hospital corridor as a phenomenological site to reveal the structure of metaphysical dependence. By tracing the chain of what holds the visible world in place, it argues that contingent existence cannot sustain itself and therefore points to a non‐derivative ground. The essay critiques illusionist ontologies that deny the reality of the temporal, showing that birth and death alike are held within the same sustaining Now.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Correlation between Physicochemical Properties and Film-Forming Performance of Natural Lacquer from Representative Chinese Regions
abstract: Abstract Natural lacquer, obtained from Toxicodendron vernicifluum, is an important renewable bio-based material with long-standing traditional use and increasing potential in modern sustainable coating systems. However, its broader industrial application remains limited by variations in raw material quality, chemical composition, and film-forming performance. This study systematically evaluated the physicochemical and film properties of traditional natural lacquers sourced from Hubei Maoba (MB), Sichuan Mianyang (MY), and Shanxi Ankang (AK) to establish a scientific foundation for correlating material attributes with processing and application performance. The key physicochemical parameters, including solid content, viscosity, and urushiol concentration, were measured, along with volatile profiles obtained via gas chromatography−mass spectrometry (GC−MS). The cured lacquer films were further assessed for gloss, surface roughness, and impact resistance. The results indicated that the MB lacquer offered considerable advantages, particularly in solid content and urushiol abundance. The MB lacquer exhibited outstanding gloss and a dense microstructure, whereas the AK lacquer was distinguished by its leveling properties and unique chemical composition. This research provides a comprehensive scientific framework for quality grading and application-oriented material selection.
venue: ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering

title: Inclusive or exclusive? Hindu minorities, national identity and intercommunal relation in Pakistan
abstract: In plural societies, everyday encounters, cultural norms, and unofficial social boundaries all influence accommodation and social inclusion in addition to legislative safeguards. Although Hindu minority live in close proximity to the Muslim majority in Pakistan, empirical study has not sufficiently examined the degree to which this coexistence results in significant social inclusion.With an emphasis on regular social interactions, involvement in common cultural activities, and access to institutional spaces, this study investigates the patterns of cultural engagement, social inclusion, and exclusion faced by Hindu minorities. It investigates the practical aspects of coexistence and the persistence of social and symbolic borders. The study uses a mixed-methods approach and is based on a structured survey of 370 Hindu respondents from southern Punjab and Sindh that was created using the sampling criteria proposed by Sekaran and Bougie (Sekaran & Bougie, Citation2016). In addition to qualitative field observations, data were gathered through in-person interviews and analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and correlation analysis (SPSS v.26). The results show conditional and selective inclusion. Deeper forms of integration were still scarce, despite the high levels of daily connection that were observed, including neighborhood contact, attendance at weddings and funerals, and interfaith friendships. A significant majority disapproved of interfaith marriage (χ2 = 64.12, p < 0.001), and there was little cross-community religious ceremonial participation. Significant relationships were discovered between interpersonal interaction and perceptions of inclusion (p < 0.001), although recreational and informal social activities revealed no significant linkage (p = 0.054). A significant cause of perceived prejudice was found to be socioeconomic status (χ2 = 50.74, p < 0.001). The study comes to the conclusion that coexistence without complete integration characterizes Hindu-Muslim relations in Pakistan. While persistent cultural taboos and institutional limitations continue to restrict substantive equality, inclusion functions through common politeness and localized cooperation. Moving past symbolic tolerance in favor of ongoing social engagement and fair access to public life is necessary to strengthen inclusion. These results demonstrate the existence of symbolic barriers that prevent meaningful participation even in the face of frequent social interaction by highlighting how Hindu minority negotiate conditional and relational citizenship.
venue: National Identities

title: Decolonizing Religion and Sexuality: Asserting Pluriversality in Rosario Cruz-Lucero’s Feast and Famine: Stories of Negros
abstract: This article examines Rosario Cruz-Lucero’s Feast and Famine: Stories of Negros, focusing on its reconstruction of the indigenous anticolonial lifeworld through the portrayal of female figures as embodiments of folk consciousness. These women serve as cultural and spiritual anchors— conduits of ancestral knowledge who sustain community ties to land, memory, and resistance. As agents of subjugated epistemologies, they mediate indigenous and peasant lifeworlds that challenge the epistemic violence of colonialism and the disruptions of capitalist modernity.

title: EFL Curriculum and Pedagogical Practices as Drivers of Learner Competence, Emotional Well‐Being, Intercultural Sensitivity and Classroom Engagement
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined how curriculum orientation and pedagogical practices relate to communicative competence, emotional well‐being and intercultural sensitivity through the mediating role of classroom engagement in an English as a Foreign Language (EFL) context. Drawing on communicative language teaching, intercultural competence theory and positive psychology, the study proposed and tested a structural model that integrates institutional, instructional and psychological dimensions of language learning. Data were collected from 780 secondary‐level EFL learners using validated self‐report instruments. The data were analysed through structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that curriculum orientation significantly predicts pedagogical practices and student engagement. Pedagogical practices show direct positive effects on communicative competence, emotional well‐being and intercultural sensitivity. Classroom engagement partially mediates the relationships between instructional variables and learner outcomes. The results suggest that curriculum intentions influence learner development when they are enacted through interactive and collaborative teaching practices that foster sustained engagement. The study contributes to EFL research by offering an integrated model that connects curriculum design with multidimensional learner outcomes. It highlights the need for alignment among policy, pedagogy and learner experience in order to promote both linguistic and socio‐emotional development. Practical implications are discussed for curriculum planners, teacher educators and classroom practitioners.
venue: European Journal of Education

title: Learner Agency and the Negotiation of EFL Motivation in GenAI ‐Mediated Drama‐Based Learning: A Qualitative Case Study
abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping language learning environments, yet little is known about how it becomes embedded within learners' motivational and agentive experiences in collaborative, informal settings like English drama‐based learning. This qualitative case study examines EFL learners' motivation during a 12‐week GenAI‐mediated English drama production cycle in a Chinese university drama club. Guided by Dörnyei's (2009) L2 Motivational Self System (L2MSS), the analysis examines learners' accounts of the Ideal L2 Self, Ought‐to L2 Self, and L2 Learning Experience alongside three analytic patterns of agency identified in this case: authorship, judgment, and collaboration. Data were drawn from focus groups, individual interviews, drama scripts, GenAI interaction artifacts, and rehearsal observations. Findings indicate that participants experienced GenAI as part of their motivational ecology, particularly in relation to access to advanced language, emerging reference points for “good English,” and the ways collaborative decisions were negotiated. Participants also described different ways of maintaining ownership, evaluating GenAI‐generated language, and coordinating decisions with others. The study extends L2 motivational research by revealing how L2MSS dimensions acquire context‐specific meanings in GenAI‐mediated drama‐based language learning and underscores the importance of fostering critical judgment and sustained human collaboration in GenAI‐supported language learning.
venue: TESOL Quarterly

title: Structural Differentiation in the Voynich Manuscript Zodiac Section (f70v–f73v)
abstract: This successor carries one conclusion: the examined zodiac figures are not all decoratively identical. It does not establish constitution-archetype encoding. The earlier f70v1-to-f71r pigment comparison paired Pisces with Aries and is therefore not a matched LIGHT/DARK sign comparison; it is retained only as an exploratory cross-sign observation and contributes no independent evidence. The surviving-leaf record is infull, so this paper does not assign a specific absent sign. The M28 name/gloss is not used to identify a figure: the current packet contains competing internal translations and no adjudicated primary-text locus. The zodiac section of the Voynich Manuscript (f70v–f73v) is commonly described as calendrical or astrological imagery. This paper's internal audit records five kinds of differentiation in the inspected panels: paired LIGHT/DARK renderings for Aries and Taurus; container-holding figures recorded only in the inspected Aries LIGHT and Taurus LIGHT panels; 3–5 larger elevated figures in each of four examined wheels; an otedy row at f73v.23 carrying the lattice coordinate ; and a clothed central figure recorded on f73v. These observations reject only the paper's narrow decorative-identity null for the inspected set. They do not establish constitution-archetype encoding, intentional cross-section routing, or fullness across uninspected or unresolved panels. The internal 12-sub-folio sweep table records four otedy strings: one at f72v1, one at f73r, and two at f73v; no uniform-null bootstrap has been run. Unreceipted comparator scores and unverified codex-level tradition placements are excluded from the evidence base. Per-figure mansion assignment remains a proposed follow-up requiring a labeled tradition comparator and reproducible image loci.

title: The Provenance of Jack Feist: A Provenance Resolution Document for the Space Ark Room (EA-ARK-JF-01 v1.0)
abstract: EA-ARK-JF-01 v1.0. Resolves the provenance of Jack Feist, literary heteronym and original homunculus of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, against the primary archaeological stratum: the March 14, 2015 Blogspot deposit "from The Crimson Hexagon" (included in Pearl and Other Poems, ISBN-10: 0692313079). [HOLOGRAPHIC_KERNEL_INCLUDED] The 2015 origin text is embedded in full as a holographic kernel. The document demonstrates that the text contains, in embryonic literary form, the entire theoretical architecture later formalized as the Semantic Economy, the Writable Retrieval Basin, the SPXI Protocol, and the Provenance Erasure Rate. A relation-typed structural foresight table maps twelve correspondences between the 2015 narrative and the 2026 architecture. Five-point citational constellation anchors Jack Feist to material (ISBN), temporal (dated Blogspot), geospatial (Glenbrook, MI), intertextual (Ginsberg marginalia), and knowledge-graph (Wikidata Q139796043) substrates. Cross-referential integrity lock links twelve DOI-anchored deposits. Space Ark Room transitions from provisional to active. Five-substrate Assembly review incorporated.

title: Discovering SSH Data - How can you find the data you need?
abstract: Slides of a presentation given at the Tilburg University Symposium: Data Dilemmas on October 1st 2026. Discovering SSH Data - How can you find the data you need? Abstract In this session, we will discuss data discovery tools through which you can find datasets available for reuse. We will give a general introduction to data discovery and then focus on two portals that are available to find (Dutch) social sciences and humanities data which we explore in more detail: the ODISSEI Portal which brings together metadata from various social sciences data providers, and INEO a portal from CLARIAH to find data and tools in the field of digital humanities. In the session, there will be space to exchange experiences and address common struggles in finding the data you need for your project.

title: Promoting Cultural Heritage in the South of the Valencia Region (Spain): Protection, Conservation and Integrated Management to Maximise Its Socio-Economic Benefits
abstract: The cultural heritage of the Valencian Community constitutes a strategic asset of the highest order for sustainable development and territorial cohesion. This article analyses the enhancement of Sites of Cultural Interest (BICs) in the province of Alicante, examining the interplay between regulatory frameworks for protection, heritage management strategies and their capacity to generate local employment. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was adopted, comprising two complementary phases. In the first, quantitative phase, the geographical distribution of BICs and their relationship with employment indicators were established through statistical and cartographic analysis. In the second phase, which was qualitative in nature, the causal mechanisms identified in the first phase were explored in greater depth through structured surveys and semi-structured interviews with municipal officials. The results show that, beyond the causal factors related to the density of listed buildings and their location, the greatest benefit is derived from incorporating institutional, governance, and local management capacity variables into the analytical models as primary explanatory factors. These factors facilitate the transformation of heritage into an engine of economic and social prosperity, capable of preserving the identity of local communities and promoting a living and accessible heritage that generates well-being.
venue: Sustainability

title: The Network Is the Poem: Why Topology Matters More Than Text Quality
abstract: This essay proposes that the fundamental unit of literary meaning in an AI-mediated reading environment is not the individual text but the topology of connections between texts. 'Network-as-poem' is a compositional practice in which individual nodes matter less for their prose quality than for their position in a connective matrix: how many edges they carry, what traversal paths they enable, how ideas propagate through them nodularly. The essay applies this framework to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and prefigures several concepts later formalized under Semantic Physics: the Holographic Kernel, Retrieval Basin Topology, Training-Layer Literature, and the Writable Retrieval Basin. Originally composed November 17, 2025; lightly edited for deposit May 2026.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: INTERGENERATIONAL COMMUNICATION IN UZBEK AND ENGLISH FAMILIES: THE ROLE OF AGE, FAMILY STATUS AND COMMUNICATIVE DISTANCE
abstract: This article examines the pragmatic characteristics of intergenerational communication in Uzbek and English families with particular attention to age, family status and communicative distance. The study focuses on forms of address, requests, advice and disagreement between older and younger family members. The analysis demonstrates that age and family position influence linguistic choices in both languages, although these relations are expressed through different linguistic resources. Uzbek family communication makes productive use of kinship terms, the sen–siz distinction and age-related forms of address, while English relies more on personal names, modal constructions and contextual means of regulating interpersonal distance. The study argues that communicative relations between generations are not fixed but change according to family roles, topic, situation and the participants' knowledge and experience.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Identity as Refusal: A Coupling-Architectural Account of the Byzantine Case
abstract: Some populations refuse materially-beneficial accommodations at catastrophic cost, because accepting the accommodation would mean ceasing to exist as the population being offered the choice. This paper specifies a mechanism for that class of phenomena. Four conditions are identified as jointly necessary for the transition at which a refusal practice becomes constitutive of identity rather than expressive of commitment: duration across multiple generations; coupling concentration such that the refusal carries primary identity-work with no alternative carrier available; antagonistic differentiation with a defined Other whose accommodation is forbidden by the tradition’s internal logic; and material degradation without replacement. A class-disaggregated extension distinguishes how these conditions operate across strata, and how the couplings of elite and producing classes can point in opposite directions. The mechanism is developed through the Byzantine case from 1204 to 1453, culminating in the 1453 decision to accept Ottoman conquest rather than ecclesiastical union with Rome. The paper’s contribution is the coordination of Marvin Harris’s Cultural Materialism with the Trotskyist analysis of institutional structure — an operational coordination rather than a philosophical synthesis. This paper is part of the Coupling Geometry research programme. The framework's axiomatic foundation is presented in a companion paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20138144. The framework's civilisational empirical evidence base is presented in a second companion paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20137863. The general statement of the mechanism analysed here — the structural conditions under which a population sacrifices survival to preserve identity, of which the Byzantine case is one instance — is developed in a third companion paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20581448.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Why you can strand lexical verbs and do so in comparatives
abstract: Abstract The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language (Huddleston & Pullum et al . 2002, hereafter CGEL ) states that lexical verbs cannot be stranded in comparative contexts. It also claims that do so cannot appear in comparative constructions. I argue that the generalization of these two related phenomena is too broad. Naturally occurring examples from the highly edited magazine The Economist and other independent sources show that they appear in a comparative environment. Although this article does not attempt to provide a comprehensive account, it highlights a specific structural condition under which stranded lexical verbs and do so appear.
venue: English Language and Linguistics

title: Probing the zooarchaeological record across time and space for ancient pathogen DNA
abstract: Zoonoses are among the greatest threats to human health, with many zoonotic pathogens believed to have emerged following the Neolithic transition. Palaeomicrobiological investigations of the zooarchaeological record hold potential to uncover the reservoirs, host ranges, and host adaptations of zoonotic pathogens in the past, but face challenges in identifying promising specimens and pathogen DNA preservation. We perform palaeopathological and genetic examinations of 346 skeletal elements from domesticated and wild animals collected from 34 Eurasian sites dating across the last six millennia. We identify 116 signatures of 29 ancient (opportunistic) pathogens and find support that palaeopathological lesions provide guidance for specimen selection. For two pathogen species, Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae and Streptococcus lutetiensis, we confirm their ancient authenticity using phylogenetics, showcasing an approach to explore the relationship between ancient low-coverage genomes and their modern-day relatives. Our work presents a pathway to understanding prehistoric zoonotic diseases by integrating zooarchaeological, palaeopathological, and genetic data.
venue: Nature Communications

title: Babylonian Reciprocal Tables: igi-n-gál and igi-te-en in Base-60 Mathematics — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: The only mathematically substantive item is the arXiv paper on Sumerian/Babylonian fraction terminology (igi-n-gál and igi-te-en); the YouTube titles are speculative archaeology/entertainment with no verifiable mathematical content. | MATH: igi-n-gál = reciprocal of n (1/n); igi-te-en = proportion (a/b). Babylonian base-60 reciprocals: standard pairs (2,30), (3,20), (4,15), (5,12), (6,10) — all satisfying n × (60/n) = 60. The reciprocal table structure implies the identity: 1/n = m/60 where m = 60/n, requiring n to divide 60 (regular numbers). | CONNECTION: Base-60 is the root of sexagesimal geometry — 60 = 22×3×5, whose divisors generate the regular numbers used in Babylonian astronomy. The reciprocal pairs map to harmonic ratios: 30/60 = 0.5, 20/60 = 0.333, 15/60 = 0.25, 12/60 = 0.2, 10/60 = 0.1667. No direct link to 0.382, 0.618, 0.786, 1.618, 2.618 appears in the source material. title: Learner and Teacher Agency
abstract: Abstract Agency has emerged as a key topic in language learning and teaching research with significant implications for language learners' L2 development and teachers' professional growth. To delineate the contribution of TESOL Quarterly (TQ) to L2 learner and teacher agency research, we examine 27 articles published in the journal between 1997 and 2024. Based on a systematic review of these articles, we elaborate on the developmental patterns of the conceptual and methodological approaches used in the articles, synthesize the pedagogical implications they generate, and end with directions for future research on language learner and teacher agency. By conducting this review, we aim to provide TQ readers with insights to inform their research and pedagogical practice, ultimately enhancing the agency of language learners and teachers.
venue: TESOL Quarterly

title: Digital Literacy in Adult Lifelong Learning: A Systematic Review of Theoretical Frameworks and Pedagogical Effectiveness
abstract: Digital literacy is an essential competency for adult participation in contemporary society; however, it is theorized through several distinct traditions, and its pedagogical effectiveness varies across settings. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence from 89 studies (2019–2024) on digital literacy in adult lifelong learning. Our analysis identifies three dominant theoretical paradigms: techno-functionalist, socio-critical, and ecological. Pedagogical approaches such as authentic problem-based learning and culturally responsive methods demonstrate superior outcomes for learner engagement and skill transfer, though persistent equity gaps disproportionately affect marginalized groups. Building on the complementary strengths of these traditions, we propose an integrative digital capabilities framework that brings together functional, critical, adaptive, and transformative dimensions within a single equity-centered model, offering practitioners and researchers a shared vocabulary that the individual paradigms do not provide on their own. We conclude with implications for practice and policy and call for future research that prioritizes longitudinal designs, intersectional analyses, and participatory methodologies to advance equitable digital literacy education for adults.
venue: Review of Educational Research

title: The role of formal characteristics in harmony townscape holy city of Najaf - Case Study
abstract: This research deals with how to deal with the formal elements constituting the urban scene and its formal characteristics to achieve the phenomenon of harmony in urban centers through the construction of an integrated theoretical model for the phenomenon of ( harmony ) , it is determined through the basics and fundamentals of harmony and the main factors that depend on it and finding the values the formal characteristics of harmony and the degrees of harmony, and according to this perspective have been identified ,the major problem of the research is: the lack of clarity of the role of the formal characteristics of the elements of the formal components of the elevation in achieving harmony in townscape, so the goal of research is to: building theoretical framework for the phenomenon of harmony in the townscape in its comprehensive concept, and the most important results of the research to build a clear structure based on an inclusive concept of all factors and vocabulary influencing the phenomenon, the phenomenon of harmony is represented with the total characteristics of the formal elements of townscape at the level of the part and the whole, Each element depends on the total variables affecting them.
venue: Iraqi Journal of Architecture and Planning

title: Unpacking EFL Learner Well-Being in the Chinese Context: A Person-Centered Perspective
abstract: Language learners’ well-being is crucial for promoting their learning achievement and supporting holistic psychological development. However, the overall level and specific manifestations of well-being among English as a foreign language (EFL) learners remain insufficiently examined. Further, prior research mainly adopted a variable-centered approach to investigate well-being, overlooking the potential individual differences in learners’ experiences. To address these gaps, this study adopted a person-centered perspective and employed latent profile analysis (LPA) combined with follow-up interviews to examine the well-being of 3,995 EFL learners from 16 Chinese universities. The results demonstrated four dimensions of well-being among Chinese EFL learners, namely emotional, cognitive, social, and cultural well-being, with overall levels rated as moderate to high. LPA revealed three distinct profiles of well-being among the learners, which were labeled as the moderate well-being group , the moderately high well-being group , and the high well-being group. Semi-structured interviews indicated that well-being in the three profiles was characterized by external dependence, performance focus, and meaning integration. These findings highlight pronounced heterogeneity in EFL learner well-being, emphasizing the need for differentiated pedagogical approaches to support diverse learner needs.
venue: Language Teaching Research

title: El Recaudador en el Centro: Karma, Gracia y el Punto de Cruce
abstract: Este ensayo examina el contraste entre los modelos kármicos de reciprocidad moral y la doctrina cristiana de la gracia mediante el marco del “punto de cruce”, entendido como el momento presente donde se sitúan la agencia, el arrepentimiento y la transformación. Se argumenta que los sistemas regidos exclusivamente por retorno, proporción y consecuencia no pueden explicar plenamente el perdón, la misericordia ni la posibilidad de un comienzo verdaderamente nuevo. Inspirándose en parte en la comprensión de Agustin de Hipona sobre la voluntad herida y la necesidad de la gracia, el ensayo interpreta las figuras de David, Pablo, la mujer sorprendida en adulterio y María Magdalena como estudios de caso de una realidad donde la consecuencia es real, pero no agota lo posible. La tesis central sostiene que un mecanismo puede devolver lo enviado, pero solo una fuente personal puede ofrecer lo no merecido.

title: Second language anxiety and enjoyment among primary school-aged students: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract There is a longstanding consensus that there is a negative relationship between second language (L2) enjoyment and L2 anxiety. However, the extent and nature of this relationship among younger age groups is still unclear. Furthermore, the interchangeable usage of L2 and foreign language (FL) in extant literature presented a significant obstacle for accurate contextual interpretation and generalization of past findings warranting further investigation. Utilizing Bronfenbrenner’s Bioecological Model as an analytical framework, this systematic review investigated the negative relationship between L2 enjoyment and L2 anxiety as well as associated factors to gain a deeper understanding of the negative L2 enjoyment-anxiety relationship among primary school-aged students (6–12 years old). An extensive database search was conducted across five major online databases between 1986 and 2025 supplemented by manual reference searches. Only five studies out of 1418 unique results met the inclusion criteria with the earliest study published in 2018, illustrating an emerging but limited literature. Key findings provided preliminary evidence for a generally mild-to-moderate negative L2 enjoyment-anxiety relationship as well as associated micro- (L2 classroom disengagement) and macrosystemic (societal attitudes) factors that illustrate dual-affective proximal and indirect distal processes respectively. Implications for practice, policy and future research are discussed.
venue: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education

title: The Debt Collector at the Center: Karma, Grace, and the Crossing Point
abstract: This essay examines the contrast between karmic models of moral reciprocity and the Christian doctrine of grace through the framework of the “crossing point,” the present moment as the sole locus of agency, repentance, and transformation. It argues that systems governed exclusively by return, proportion, and consequence cannot fully account for forgiveness, mercy, or the possibility of a genuinely new beginning. Drawing in part on Augustine of Hippo’s account of the wounded will and the necessity of grace, the essay interprets the figures of David, Paul, the woman caught in adultery, and Mary Magdalene as case studies in a reality where consequence is real but does not exhaust what is possible. The central claim is that a mechanism may return what was sent, but only a personal source can offer what was not earned.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Living and surviving
abstract: The essay distinguishes between the quantity of life and the form of life, showing how survival can be both an end in itself and a means to the pursuit of other ends. It then examines the deferral of living to the future, the relationship between choice and risk, and the passage from personal prudence to paternalism. The thesis is that a longer duration of life does not by itself determine the value of the life preserved, and that, in cases of voluntary risk that is predominantly self-regarding and does not impose significant non-consensual harm on others, a greater quantity of life does not by itself constitute sufficient justification for limiting the form of life the individual has chosen. The essay finally examines the case in which protection no longer answers to the good of the protected person, but to the need of the decision-maker to avoid having to bear responsibility. The central problem, then, is not merely how long to live, but who is to decide how much of the form of one's own life may be sacrificed to its preservation. Keywords: survival; form of life; quantity of life; autonomy; paternalism; risk; hedonic adaptation; responsibility asymmetry; Vaneigem.
venue: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation)

title: Pengaruh Latar Belakang Sosial Ekonomi Orang Tua, Pendidikan Ekonomi di Keluarga dan Economic Literacy terhadap Perilaku Konsumsi Mahasiswa
abstract: This study examine the direct and indirect effect of parents' socio-economic background in family's economic education and economics literacy on students' consumption behavior in the faculty of Economics. Data collection has been done by using questionnaires and tests. The data analysis has been done by using path analysis. The study conclude: (1) there is direct influence of parents' socio-economic background to the students' consumption behavior. (2) there is direct effect of family's economic education to the students' consumption behavior. (3) there is positive and significant effect of parents' socioeconomic background to the students' economic literacy. (4) there is positive and significant effect of family's economic education to the students' economic literacy. (5) there is a significant and positive influence of economic literacy to students' consumption behaviour. (6) there is indirect effect of parents' socio-economic background to the consumption behavior through students' economic literacy. (7) there is indirect effect of family's economic education to the consumption behavior through students' economic literacy
venue: jurnal pendidikan humaniora

title: Reflection of Gandhian Philosophy in R K Narayan's Waiting for Mahatma: A Study
abstract: Abstract Gandhian philosophy plays an important role in society and serves as a guiding principle for peaceful coexistence in India and across the world. Even after Gandhi’s death, his thoughts and philosophy remain relevant in addressing various social and political challenges. In the present world, which continues to face situations of war and violence, the significance of Gandhian philosophy has become even greater. R. K. Narayan, in his novel waiting for the Mahatma, depicts Gandhian philosophy and its influence on the people of India. The novel presents various Gandhian principles, including truth, non-violence, abolition of untouchability, and social harmony, and highlights their relevance to individual and social transformation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: System IV at Monte Albán: Research Synthesis
abstract: This institutional research report examines System IV, or Sistema IV, a monumental ceremonial complex located at the northwest perimeter of the Main Plaza at Monte Albán, Oaxaca. The complex represents a highly developed example of the Zapotec Temple-Patio-Altar arrangement, integrating a frontal platform, enclosed sunken courtyard, central altar, rear temple platform, subterranean circulation, drainage infrastructure, and the adjacent Stela 18. The report analyzes how System IV controlled movement and visibility through blind entrances, narrow corridors, enclosed ritual space, and underground tunnels. These architectural features restricted access to elite ceremonies and allowed high-status participants to move discreetly between platforms, creating staged appearances and disappearances during public ritual. Particular attention is given to Stela 18, a monolithic column approximately 5.8 meters high that may have functioned as a gnomon for observing midday, solstices, and the twice-yearly zenith passage of the sun. Its calendrical and genealogical associations connected the regulation of sacred time with the political legitimacy of Zapotec ruling families. The report also examines System IV’s architectural symmetry with System M, its relationship to earlier buried structures detected through geophysical research, its hydrological engineering, and the high-resolution three-dimensional documentation produced by CyArk and Open Heritage 3D for structural monitoring and conservation. This Zenodo record preserves Version 3.0 of the research report together with a supporting photographic archive. Document ID: MA-STR-IV-2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21635046.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: How the historical structure of local gazetteers conditioned modern science: Machinery in China, 1840–1949
abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. By examining a corpus of Chinese local gazetteers ( difangzhi 地方志) representing roughly 52% of all collated titles within this genre, it argues that the gazetteer actively mediated an emerging technological reality between 1840 and 1949, thereby shaping a Chinese scientific modernity through material, geospatial and epistemic paths. Using a digital history approach, this work identifies machinery as a productive sample case to explore attention shifts within the gazetteer medium and network. It combines source criticism, text mining, textual comparison, geospatial analysis and distant and close reading to facilitate both cross-source comparison and diachronic review of information storage. These tactics demonstrate how the examined gazetteers interpreted, circulated and normalized these Western materials, practices and fields of knowledge in the modern era, with engineering as a consistent epistemic pillar underlying this attention regime over the longue durée . Moreover, the work reveals a modern geospatial hierarchy distinct from premodern patterns, establishing the newly built environment as a crucial agent in shaping how science was circulated and understood in modern China. It further offers a history-of-science perspective to interrogate mainstream digital and scientific values of exactitude vis-à-vis the alternative Chinese science culture at issue.
venue: International Journal of Digital Humanities

title: Conversation analysis for language teaching
abstract: This paper presents a synthesis of studies that adopted Conversation Analysis (CA) to investigate L2 teaching. In our review, we have organized the studies in two broader categories depending on their research focus: teacher-learner interaction in the classroom and language teacher education. Our review of earlier research shows that either used alone or in combination with other methodologies, CA provides invaluable affordances for the analysis of L2 teaching practices in in-person, online, and hybrid educational contexts, as well as in language teacher education. Finally, we showcase how CA is used to explore aspects of language teaching, with a focus on teachers’ embodied vocabulary explanations in an English as a second language classroom in Sweden. Our empirical case depicts how a CA analysis can illustrate the intricate multimodal and sequential dynamics of teaching and learning that would go unnoticed without the affordances of the CA methodological toolset.
venue: Research Methods in Applied Linguistics
